scenario: 你要给一个日活千万的 Web 应用写请求代码，工期两周，不可能自己实现丢包重传。
scenario_en: You have two weeks to ship request code for a web app with ten million daily users, so reimplementing packet retransmission yourself is off the table.
q: 网络分层（OSI 模型）对应用开发者的根本意义是什么？
q_en: What is the core value of network layering, or the OSI model, for application developers?
options: 规定了所有协议的字节格式
分层是抽象：只需和下一层打交道
让网络传输更快
强制所有系统用 7 层协议
why: 分层就是抽象——像用语言里的 open 而不是手动指挥磁盘读字节。请求网页时你不需要懂物理层，只要会用下一层即可。
why_en: Network layers are abstractions that let developers reason about communication at their own level without knowing how lower layers move the bits.
diagram:
flowchart TB
    A["应用层 L7"] --> B["传输层 L4"]
    B --> C["网络层 L3"]
    C --> D["更底层细节"]
    A -.只依赖下一层.-> B
options_en: It dictates the exact byte format every protocol must use.
Layering is an abstraction — you deal only with the layer below you.
It makes network transmission inherently faster.
It forces every system to implement all seven OSI layers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把网络通信拆成 7 层的参考模型，每层只依赖它下面那一层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OSI is the reference model that splits network communication into seven layers, each depending only on the layer below it.

optionExplanations: 分层从没规定过字节格式，那是具体协议自己的事，分层只是把复杂度切开。
分层的价值就是抽象——你只需要弄懂和你相邻的下一层，不用管物理层怎么搬比特。
分层不会让传输本身变快，它换来的是可维护性和职责隔离，不是性能。
没有系统被强制走满 7 层，很多实现会跳过或合并某些层。
optionExplanations_en: layering never dictates byte formats; that's each protocol's own job, layering just splits up complexity.
layering's value is abstraction — you only need the layer right below you, not how bits move on the wire.
layering doesn't speed up transmission itself; it buys maintainability, not performance.
no system is forced to implement all seven layers; real stacks skip or merge layers freely.

q: 补全面试最常涉及的三个网络层：
q_en: Fill in the three network layers that come up most often in interviews.
text: 第 3 层网络层：{{IP}}，负责路由与寻址；第 4 层传输层：{{TCP}}、UDP、QUIC，提供端到端通信；第 7 层应用层：DNS、{{HTTP}}（浏览器加载网页、调用 REST API 用的请求-响应协议）、WebSocket、WebRTC。
why: 面试聚焦三层：L3 管「送到哪台机器」，L4 管「可靠性/顺序等端到端保证」，L7 是开发者天天用的应用协议。
why_en: Interviews focus on layer three with IP for routing, layer four with TCP and UDP for end-to-end guarantees, and layer seven application protocols like HTTP.

scenario: 排查跨机房服务调用：包都到了但顺序全乱，你要定位这属于哪一层该管的事。
scenario_en: You're debugging cross-datacenter service calls where every packet arrives but the order is scrambled, and you need to know which layer owns that.
q: 网络层（L3）的 IP 协议负责什么？
q_en: What is IP responsible for at the network layer, or L3?
options: 保证数据按序到达
加密通信内容
给每个包标上源/目的地址并逐跳路由，尽力而为投递（不保证送达和顺序）
维护客户端与服务器的会话
why: IP 只管寻址和路由：每个包独立转发、尽力送达，不保证可靠或有序——所以场景里的乱序问题归 L4（TCP）管。把应用数据切成段是 TCP 做的，IP 只在包超过链路 MTU 时做分片。
why_en: IP only handles addressing and routing: each packet is forwarded independently, best-effort, with no reliability or ordering guarantee, so the reordering in the scenario is L4's (TCP's) job. Segmenting application data is TCP's work; IP only fragments packets that exceed a link's MTU.
options_en: It guarantees packets arrive in order.
It encrypts the contents of the communication.
It stamps each packet with source/destination addresses and routes it hop by hop, best-effort (no delivery or ordering guarantee).
It maintains session state between client and server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层协议，负责给数据包寻址并在网络间转发、尽力而为地投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer protocol that addresses packets and forwards them across networks on a best-effort basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: OSI 模型里负责路由和寻址的网络层，主角是 IP。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 3, the network layer, handles routing and addressing and is dominated by IP.

optionExplanations: 按序到达是 L4（TCP）的职责，IP 本身不做排序或重传保证。
加密属于更上层（如 TLS），IP 只负责路由寻址，不碰内容加解密。
IP 的职责就是给每个包标上地址、逐跳路由并尽力投递，可靠性和顺序留给上层去做。
会话状态由应用层或传输层维护，IP 是无状态的逐包转发。
optionExplanations_en: ordered delivery is TCP's job at L4 — IP makes no ordering or retransmission promise.
encryption belongs to a higher layer like TLS; IP only routes and addresses, never touches content.
IP's job is addressing each packet and routing it hop by hop on a best-effort basis, leaving reliability and ordering to the layer above.
session state is tracked by transport or application layers, not by stateless, per-packet IP.

scenario: 你的服务直接基于 IP 收发，拿到的是一堆乱序、可能重复的包，要决定补哪一层。
scenario_en: Your service talks straight over IP and gets back an unordered, possibly duplicated pile of packets, so you have to decide which layer to add.
q: 传输层（L4）在网络层之上补充了什么？
q_en: What does the transport layer, or L4, add on top of the network layer?
options: 端到端通信服务：可靠性、有序性等特性
域名解析：把主机名翻译成目标 IP 地址
HTML 页面渲染引擎
物理层的信号调制与编码
why: L3 只把包尽力扔到目的地；TCP/QUIC/UDP 这层决定要不要在其上提供可靠、有序、流控等保证——否则你拿到的就是一堆乱序的包。
why_en: The transport layer adds end-to-end services like reliability, ordering, and flow control on top of the network layer's raw packet delivery.
options_en: End-to-end services like reliability and ordering.
Resolving a hostname into a destination IP address.
The browser's HTML rendering engine.
Modulating and encoding the physical-layer signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: OSI 模型里提供端到端保证（可靠性、顺序、流控）的传输层，主角是 TCP/UDP/QUIC。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 4, the transport layer, provides end-to-end guarantees like reliability, ordering, and flow control, dominated by TCP, UDP, and QUIC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 构建在 UDP 之上的现代传输协议，提供接近 TCP 的可靠性但性能更好、采用率还不够广。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QUIC is a modern transport protocol built on UDP that offers TCP-like reliability with better performance but is not yet as widely adopted.

optionExplanations: 传输层在 L3 之上加了端到端保证——要不要可靠、要不要保序，由 TCP/UDP/QUIC 决定。
域名解析是 DNS 在应用层做的事，跟传输层没关系。
HTML 渲染发生在浏览器的应用层，传输层根本看不到内容格式。
物理信号调制属于物理层（L1），传输层只处理逻辑上的字节流。
optionExplanations_en: the transport layer adds end-to-end guarantees above L3 — TCP, UDP, or QUIC decide reliability and ordering.
domain resolution is DNS's job at the application layer, unrelated to transport.
HTML rendering happens in the browser's application layer; transport never sees content format.
signal modulation belongs to the physical layer (L1); transport only handles logical byte streams.

scenario: 设计一个浏览器聊天应用，你只在应用层选协议，传输层的事交给下面的 TCP/UDP。
scenario_en: You're designing a browser chat app and only pick protocols at the application layer, leaving transport concerns to TCP or UDP underneath.
q: 以下哪组全是应用层（L7）协议？
q_en: Which group contains only application-layer, or L7, protocols?
options: IP、InfiniBand（网络层）
TCP、UDP、QUIC（传输层）
SYN、ACK、FIN、RST（TCP 报文标志位）
DNS、HTTP、WebSocket、WebRTC
why: DNS、HTTP、WebSocket、WebRTC 都是应用层协议：HTTP/1.1、HTTP/2 和 WebSocket 跑在 TCP 上，DNS 通常走 UDP（大响应时改走 TCP），WebRTC 媒体走 UDP。SYN/ACK/FIN 只是 TCP 的报文标志。
why_en: DNS, HTTP, WebSocket and WebRTC are application-layer protocols: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and WebSocket run over TCP, DNS usually uses UDP (falling back to TCP for large responses), and WebRTC media runs over UDP. SYN/ACK/FIN are just TCP flags.
options_en: IP and InfiniBand (network layer).
TCP, UDP, and QUIC (transport layer).
SYN, ACK, FIN, and RST (TCP segment flag bits).
DNS, HTTP, WebSocket, and WebRTC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的分布式查找系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

optionExplanations: IP 和 InfiniBand 都是网络层/更底层的东西，不是应用层协议。
TCP、UDP、QUIC 是传输层协议，应用层协议是建在它们之上的。

DNS、HTTP、WebSocket、WebRTC 都跑在传输层之上，为具体应用场景提供数据抽象。

TCP, UDP, QUIC are transport protocols — application protocols are built on top of them.
SYN/ACK/FIN/RST are just flag bits inside a TCP segment, not protocols at all.
DNS, HTTP, WebSocket, and WebRTC all run above transport, giving each app its own data abstraction.

q: 把「浏览器输入 URL 到拿到网页」的步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the browser-to-webpage request flow in the correct order.
steps: TCP 三次握手建立连接
DNS 把域名解析成 IP 地址
服务器处理请求并准备响应
客户端发送 HTTP GET 请求
TCP 四次挥手关闭连接
服务器发回 HTTP 响应
why: DNS 解析 → TCP 握手 → 发请求 → 服务器处理（多数工程师唯一控制的延迟）→ 回响应 → 挥手断开。一次「简单」请求背后是多轮包交换，层层都有延迟。
why_en: A web request resolves DNS, performs the TCP handshake, sends the HTTP request, waits for server processing, receives the response, and tears the connection down.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant D as DNS
    participant S as 服务器
    C->>D: 域名解析
    D-->>C: IP 地址
    C->>S: SYN / SYN-ACK / ACK（三次握手）
    C->>S: HTTP GET
    S-->>C: HTTP 响应
    C->>S: FIN / ACK / FIN / ACK（四次挥手）

q: 补全 TCP 三次握手：
q_en: Complete the TCP three-way handshake.
text: 客户端发 {{SYN}} 请求连接；服务器回 {{SYN-ACK}} 确认请求；客户端再发 {{ACK}} 完成连接建立。断开则用 FIN/ACK/FIN/ACK 四次挥手。
why: 三次握手建立、四次挥手拆除——每个不复用连接的请求都要重复这套流程，这是后面讨论持久连接和负载均衡的伏笔。
why_en: TCP opens with a SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK three-way handshake and closes with a four-way FIN and ACK exchange.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: SYN
    S-->>C: SYN-ACK
    C->>S: ACK
    Note over C,S: 连接已建立

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP 报文里的控制标志位，分别用于发起连接、确认收到、结束连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SYN, ACK, and FIN are TCP control flags used to open a connection, acknowledge receipt, and close a connection.

scenario: 一个 API 网关每秒处理 5 万次短请求，你想把每请求的连接建立开销压下来。
scenario_en: An API gateway handles fifty thousand short requests per second, and you want to cut the per-request connection setup cost.
q: TCP 连接是客户端和服务器都要维护的状态：这一事实带来什么设计影响？
q_en: What design consequence follows from TCP connection state living on both client and server?
options: 连接一旦建立就永远免费
连接状态只由服务器端维护，客户端无需保存
不用 keep-alive 就要重建连接
TCP 连接不占用任何资源
why: 连接即状态，双方都要维护；不复用就得每请求重建，开销可观。设计实时更新类系统（持久连接）时这一点会反复出现。
why_en: Because a connection is state both sides maintain, every request repeats the costly setup unless you use keep-alive or multiplexing, which matters for realtime systems.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["请求 1"] --> B["建连"]
    B --> C["响应"]
    C --> D["断开"]
    D --> E["请求 2 再建连"]
    C -.keep-alive.-> F["复用连接"]
options_en: Once established, a connection is free forever.
The connection state is kept only on the server, and the client stores nothing.
Without keep-alive you rebuild the connection every time.
A TCP connection consumes no resources at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让一条 TCP 连接被多个 HTTP 请求复用，省去重复握手的开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP keep-alive lets one TCP connection serve multiple HTTP requests, avoiding repeated handshake overhead.

optionExplanations: 维护连接本身要占内存和文件描述符，从来不是免费的，只是分摊到了每次请求。
TCP 是双方对等维护状态，客户端和服务器都要记住序号、窗口，不是只有服务器。
连接状态双方都要维护，不复用连接（没有 keep-alive）就得每次请求重新握手，开销明显。
每条 TCP 连接都占用服务器内存和文件描述符，大量并发连接会实实在在压垮资源。
optionExplanations_en: keeping a connection alive still costs memory and file descriptors — it's amortized, not free.
TCP state is kept by both sides; client and server both track sequence numbers, not just the server.
both sides hold connection state, so without keep-alive you pay a fresh handshake on every request.
every TCP connection consumes real memory and file descriptors; enough of them exhaust resources.

scenario: 你把自建服务部署在公司内网，现在要让互联网上的外部用户直接访问它。
scenario_en: You deployed a self-hosted service inside the corporate network, and now external users on the internet need to reach it directly.
q: 关于公网 IP，正确的说法是？
q_en: Which statement about public IP addresses is correct?
options: 任何人可以随便自封公网 IP 并被全网路由
公网 IP 由 RIR 分配，全网可路由
公网 IP 只在局域网内部有效，出不了本地网络
公网 IP 由 DNS 服务器直接分配给客户端
why: 私有网络里 IP 随便定，但要让互联网流量找到你，必须用 RIR 分配的可路由地址。互联网路由基础设施针对公网 IP 之间的转发做了优化。
why_en: Public IPs are allocated by regional internet registries and are routable, so the internet backbone knows for example that addresses starting with 17 belong to Apple.
options_en: Anyone can self-assign a public IP and have it routed by the whole internet.
Public IPs are allocated by a RIR and are globally routable.
A public IP only works inside a local network and never leaves it.
Public IPs are assigned directly to clients by DNS servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层协议，负责给数据包寻址并在网络间转发、尽力而为地投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer protocol that addresses packets and forwards them across networks on a best-effort basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责分配可在公网路由的 IP 地址段的区域机构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A RIR is the regional authority that allocates blocks of publicly routable IP addresses.

optionExplanations: 自己乱定的地址不会被互联网骨干路由接受，必须走正规分配才能被全网识别。
公网 IP 由 RIR 统一分配，保证全球唯一、可被互联网路由基础设施转发。
只在局域网内有效的是私有地址段，公网 IP 恰恰是要能被外部路由的地址。
DNS 只负责把域名解析成已有的 IP，它不分配 IP 地址本身。
optionExplanations_en: a self-assigned address won't be accepted by the internet backbone without proper allocation.
public IPs are allocated by RIRs, guaranteeing global uniqueness so routing infrastructure can forward them.
addresses valid only inside a LAN are private ranges — a public IP is exactly one that routes outside.
DNS only resolves a name to an existing IP; it never assigns the IP address itself.

scenario: 为多人对战游戏选传输协议：位置更新每秒 60 次，晚到的包不如直接丢掉。
scenario_en: You're picking a transport for a multiplayer game where position updates fire sixty times a second, and a late packet is worse than a dropped one.
q: UDP 的关键特性有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which properties does UDP have?
options: 无连接：没有握手和连接建立，开销小、延迟低
不保证送达：丢包不会有任何通知
不保证顺序：包可能乱序到达
自动去重，保证恰好一次投递
why: UDP 是「机枪式」spray and pray：在 IP 之上几乎不加功能，换来速度。无连接、可能丢、可能乱序，也没有重复保护——收到的就是一坨二进制加上来源/目的地址端口。
why_en: UDP is connectionless with no handshake, offers no delivery or ordering guarantees, and has lower latency precisely because it adds so little on top of IP.
options_en: Connectionless: no handshake or setup, so overhead and latency are lower.
No delivery guarantee: a lost packet triggers no notification.
No ordering guarantee: packets can arrive out of order.
Automatic deduplication with exactly-once delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

optionExplanations: 省掉握手意味着发送前不用建立连接状态，直接把开销和延迟降到最低。
丢包发生时发送方和接收方都不会收到提示，应用层必须自己检测和处理丢失。
包可能各走各的路径，到达顺序可能和发送顺序对不上，接收方要自己排序。
UDP 不做任何去重，重复包会原样交给上层，恰好一次投递是应用自己要保证的事。
optionExplanations_en: skipping the handshake means no setup before sending, keeping overhead and latency low.
on loss, neither sender nor receiver is notified — the application must detect and handle it itself.
packets can take different paths, so arrival order can differ from send order; receivers reorder them.
UDP does no deduplication — duplicates pass straight through; exactly-once is the app's job.

scenario: 设计 VoIP 语音通话：偶尔丢一个包只是音频轻微卡顿、对话依然可懂；而等丢失的包重传到达，会让后面的新音频全部排队延迟（队头阻塞）。
scenario_en: You are designing a VoIP call: losing one audio packet causes a tiny glitch, but waiting for a lost packet to be retransmitted would hold all newer audio behind it (head-of-line blocking).
q: 传输层该选？
q_en: Which transport protocol should you choose for this VoIP audio call?
options: TCP：靠重传保证每个音频包都送达
QUIC 可靠流：每个包丢了都重传
UDP：速度优先，客户端自己扛丢包
HTTP 轮询
why: 偶发丢包只造成轻微卡顿，等重传反而让新音频排在旧包后面。UDP 不重传，客户端用抖动缓冲和丢包隐藏自己扛，换来低延迟。TCP 和 QUIC 的可靠流都会重传，同样有等待问题。
why_en: An occasional loss is a small glitch, while waiting for retransmission stalls newer audio behind the old packet. UDP doesn't retransmit; the client absorbs loss with a jitter buffer and loss concealment, gaining low latency. TCP and QUIC reliable streams both retransmit and share the waiting problem.
whenOtherWins: 数据完整性关键的场景（支付、文件传输、几乎一切非实时业务）用 TCP——凡是 UDP 不合适的地方基本都是 TCP。
options_en: TCP, retransmitting to guarantee every audio packet arrives.
QUIC reliable streams, retransmitting every lost packet.
UDP: speed over reliability, and the client absorbs the occasional loss.
HTTP polling.
tradeoff: UDP 低延迟可丢包 vs TCP 可靠重传

termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

optionExplanations: TCP 适合数据必须完整到达的场景（文件传输、支付），但这里重传会让新音频排在旧音频后面，加剧卡顿。
QUIC 的可靠流和 TCP 一样会重传每个丢失的包，同样有等待旧包的问题，不适合这里。
偶发丢包只造成轻微卡顿，等重传反而让后续音频排队；UDP 让客户端自己容忍丢包，换来实时语音要的低延迟。
轮询天然有请求间隔造成的延迟，不是持续推送，撑不起语音这种连续实时流。
optionExplanations_en: TCP suits data that must arrive whole, but retransmitting audio here queues fresh sound behind stale sound.
QUIC reliable streams retransmit every lost packet just like TCP, so they share the same wait-for-the-old-packet problem and do not fit here.
An occasional loss is a minor glitch, while waiting for retransmission queues newer audio; UDP lets the client tolerate loss and buys the low latency real-time voice needs.
Polling has built-in gaps between requests instead of continuous delivery, so it can't sustain a voice stream.

scenario: Facebook Live 的点赞刷屏要推给浏览器观众端，你想用 UDP 换更低的延迟。
scenario_en: Facebook Live reaction bursts have to reach viewers in the browser, and you want UDP to get lower latency.
q: 你想用 UDP（User Datagram Protocol）给 Facebook Live 评论的刷屏点赞做实时推送，要注意什么现实限制？
q_en: What real-world limitation matters if you want to use UDP for Facebook Live reactions in the browser?
options: UDP 无法承载表情数据
浏览器 JS 没有裸 UDP socket，只能借助 WebRTC（或较新的 WebTransport）间接用到 UDP
UDP 在蜂窝移动网络下会被运营商直接完全封锁
点赞数必须做到强一致

why_en: Browsers expose no raw UDP socket to JS; UDP is reachable only through wrapped protocols like WebRTC or WebTransport, which cost more to integrate. A common design: native apps take a realtime UDP stream while browsers fall back to batched HTTP or SSE.
options_en: UDP cannot carry emoji/reaction data.
Browser JS has no raw UDP socket; it can only reach UDP indirectly through WebRTC (or the newer WebTransport).
UDP is outright blocked by carriers on cellular mobile networks.
Like counts must be strongly consistent.

scenario: 聊天系统要求同一会话内的消息在接收端按发送顺序显示，漏一条都不行。
scenario_en: A chat system requires messages in one conversation to show up in send order on the receiving side, with none dropped.
q: TCP 的「流（stream）」意味着什么？
q_en: What does it mean that TCP exposes a stream?
options: 数据以视频流的形式传输
数据按消息块传输：接收方每次 read 正好拿到发送方一次 write 的完整内容
连接是完全无状态的
有状态连接上的有序字节流：同一连接内字节按发送顺序交付，未确认的数据会重传
why: TCP 给应用的是一条有序、可靠的字节流：双方记录序号和窗口，接收方 ACK，未确认的数据重传。它没有消息边界——应用要自己加长度前缀或分隔符来切消息。另外 TCP 是全双工，服务器本来就能随时发数据，「只能请求-响应」是 HTTP 的限制。
why_en: TCP gives the application an ordered, reliable byte stream: both sides track sequence numbers and windows, the receiver ACKs, and unacknowledged data is retransmitted. It has no message boundaries; applications add length prefixes or delimiters. TCP is also full-duplex, so a server can send at any time; request-response only is an HTTP restriction.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["发送端字节流"] --> B["TCP 分段"]
    B --> C["确认 ACK"]
    C -.丢包.-> D["重传"]
    C --> E["接收端按序读"]
options_en: Data is transmitted like a video stream.
Data moves in message units: each read on the receiver returns exactly one write from the sender.
The connection carries no state at all.
An ordered byte stream over a stateful connection: bytes on the same connection are delivered in send order, and unacknowledged data is retransmitted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。

optionExplanations: 这里的「流」指字节流这个抽象概念，跟视频流媒体没有关系。
TCP 是字节流，没有消息边界，一次 read 不一定对应一次 write；应用要自己加长度前缀或分隔符来切消息。
恰恰相反，TCP 连接是有状态的——双方要记住序号、窗口、未确认的数据。
对，TCP 在有状态连接上给应用一条有序字节流，同一连接内字节按序交付，没收到 ACK 的数据会被重传。
optionExplanations_en: 'stream' here means the byte-stream abstraction, unrelated to video streaming.
TCP is a byte stream with no message boundaries, so one read need not match one write; applications add length prefixes or delimiters to frame messages.
it's the opposite — TCP is stateful, with both sides tracking sequence numbers and unacked data.
Right: TCP gives the application an ordered byte stream over a stateful connection, delivering bytes in order and retransmitting data that was not ACKed.

scenario: 为银行转账接口选传输协议：任何一条报文丢失或乱序都会让账目算错。
scenario_en: You're choosing a transport for a bank transfer API where any lost or reordered segment corrupts the ledger.

q_en: Which properties does TCP provide?
options: 面向连接：传数据前先建立专用连接
可靠投递：保证数据按序、无错到达
流量控制防止淹没接收方 + 拥塞控制适应网络拥堵
头部固定只有 8 字节
why: TCP 四大件：面向连接、可靠有序、流控、拥塞控制——这就是它比 UDP 慢的原因，也是互联网的主力马。8 字节头是 UDP 的，TCP 头是 20-60 字节。
why_en: TCP is connection-oriented with reliable in-order delivery, flow control, and congestion control, while the tiny eight-byte header belongs to UDP.
options_en: Connection-oriented: it establishes a dedicated connection before transferring data.
Reliable delivery: it guarantees data arrives in order and without errors.
Flow control to avoid overwhelming the receiver, plus congestion control to adapt to a congested network.
A fixed 8-byte header.

optionExplanations: TCP 在传数据前先做三次握手，建立起一条双方都认可的专用连接。
TCP 靠序号和 ACK/重传机制保证数据按顺序、无差错地到达接收方。
流量控制防止发送方压垮接收方缓冲区，拥塞控制则根据网络状况动态调整发送速率。
8 字节固定头是 UDP 的特征；TCP 基础头是 20 字节，带 options 能到 60 字节。
optionExplanations_en: TCP does a three-way handshake before sending data, establishing a dedicated agreed-upon connection.
sequence numbers plus ACK-and-retransmit guarantee data arrives in order and without corruption.
flow control stops the sender overrunning the receiver's buffer; congestion control adapts send rate.
an 8-byte header is UDP's trait — TCP's base header is 20 bytes, up to 60 with options.

scenario: 你在解释实时音视频为什么常偏向 UDP：单包头部开销不是主瓶颈，但能反映协议是否在传输层替你记可靠性状态。
scenario_en: You are explaining why real-time media often leans toward UDP: packet-header overhead is not the main bottleneck, but it shows whether the transport layer tracks reliability state for you.
q: UDP/TCP 头部大小差异说明哪个传输层取舍？
q_en: What transport-layer tradeoff does the UDP/TCP header-size difference illustrate?
options: 8B vs 20-60B：少记账、低开销
20-60B vs 8B：把顺序反了
同为 20B：只按带宽选协议
无固定含义：可靠性不需要状态
why: UDP 头固定 8B；TCP 基础头 20B，带 options 可到 60B。这个数字的用途不是背诵，而是提醒你：TCP 用额外字节和状态换可靠性、流控、拥塞控制。
why_en: UDP's 8-byte header versus TCP's 20-to-60-byte header is a reminder that TCP pays extra bookkeeping for reliability, flow control, and congestion control.
options_en: 8B versus 20-60B: less bookkeeping and lower overhead.
20-60B versus 8B: the order is reversed.
Both are 20B: choose only by bandwidth.
No fixed meaning: reliability needs no state.

optionExplanations: UDP 头只需 8 字节记账，TCP 为维护可靠性状态把头部撑到 20-60 字节，这条差距就是「省记账 vs 换可靠」的体现。

两者头部大小并不相等，协议选择的关键也不是带宽，是要不要传输层帮你维护可靠性状态。
头部大小的差异恰恰说明可靠性需要额外状态字段去维护，不是无成本的。
optionExplanations_en: UDP needs only 8 bytes of bookkeeping, while TCP grows to 20-60 bytes to carry reliability state.
this swaps the two numbers — UDP is the smaller one (8B), TCP the larger (20-60B), not reversed.
the headers aren't equal, and the choice driver isn't bandwidth — it's transport-layer reliability.
the header-size gap shows reliability needs extra state fields to maintain — it isn't free.

Default to UDP because it's fast.
Default to TCP — interviewers usually assume it already.
Split every connection 50/50 between TCP and UDP.
tradeoff: 默认 TCP 省心 vs 论证清楚才切 UDP

scenario: 面试官问你为什么内部服务之间的主链路不上 QUIC，你要给出一个关于采用面成熟度的判断。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why you didn't put QUIC on the main internal service-to-service link, and you need an answer about adoption maturity.
q: 面试语境下该怎么看 QUIC？
q_en: How should you think about QUIC in interview settings?
options: 它已经完全取代了 TCP，成为新标准
基于 UDP、内置 TLS 的新传输协议，提供 TCP 式可靠性并改进了建连和队头阻塞；公网 HTTP/3 已普及，但内网服务间、负载均衡和运维工具链上 TCP 仍是默认
它只是 UDP 换了个名字，本质完全相同
它只能用于内部数据库之间的通信
why: QUIC 在 UDP 上实现了可靠流、拥塞控制和 TLS 1.3，减少建连往返和多路复用下的队头阻塞，HTTP/3 就跑在它上面。公网边缘已普遍支持，但内网服务间通信、L4 负载均衡、抓包排障工具对 TCP 的支持更成熟，所以内部主链路默认仍用 TCP。
why_en: QUIC implements reliable streams, congestion control and TLS 1.3 over UDP, cutting handshake round trips and multiplexing head-of-line blocking; HTTP/3 runs on it. It's widely supported at the public edge, but internal service links, L4 load balancers and debugging tools are more mature for TCP, so internal links still default to TCP.
options_en: It has already fully replaced TCP as the new standard.

A newer UDP-based transport with built-in TLS, giving TCP-like reliability plus faster setup and less head-of-line blocking; widely used for public HTTP/3, but TCP remains the default for internal service links, load balancers and tooling.
It's just UDP renamed, functionally identical underneath.
It's only ever used for database-to-database communication.

Right: QUIC is a standalone UDP-based transport with built-in TLS; it is widely supported at the public edge (HTTP/3), but internal service links, load balancers and tooling are more mature for TCP, so internal links still default to TCP.
QUIC is its own protocol built on UDP with its own reliability and congestion control, not a rename.
QUIC is general-purpose, used by things like HTTP/3, not specific to databases.

options: 两者都保证送达

UDP guarantees delivery, TCP is best-effort.
Neither guarantees delivery.

optionExplanations: UDP 从设计上就不做确认和重传，根本不满足「两者都保证」。
这是把两个协议的可靠性描述完全对调了，真实情况正相反。

TCP 靠 ACK 和重传保证送达，UDP 发出去就不管了，可靠性正是两者的核心差异。

this flips the two protocols' reliability descriptions — the real picture is the opposite.

TCP guarantees delivery via ACKs and retransmission, while UDP fires and forgets — that's the core gap.

scenario: 你在评估哪些业务能从 TCP 换到 UDP：有些业务宁可丢掉一点数据，也不能等 TCP 重传造成的卡顿。
scenario_en: You're evaluating which workloads can move from TCP to UDP: some of them would rather lose a little data than stall waiting for TCP retransmissions.
q: 哪些信号提示你可以选 UDP？（多选）
q_en: Which signals tell you UDP may be the right choice?
options: 低延迟是硬要求（实时应用、游戏）
能接受部分数据丢失（媒体流）
高量遥测/日志，偶尔丢一点无所谓
不需要支持浏览器，或已为浏览器准备了替代通道
why: 每一条都是独立的信号，不需要四条同时满足：A–C 说明「等重传的代价 > 丢一点数据的代价」，D 是排除障碍——浏览器没有裸 UDP 的 API（只能通过 WebRTC/QUIC 间接用）。现代应用常两者混用：视频会议用 TCP/HTTP 做信令鉴权、UDP/WebRTC 传音视频流。
why_en: Each option is an independent signal; they don't all have to hold at once. A–C mean waiting for retransmission costs more than losing some data, and D removes a blocker: browsers expose no raw UDP API (only indirectly via WebRTC/QUIC). Modern apps often mix both: TCP/HTTP for signaling and auth, UDP/WebRTC for media.
options_en: Low latency is a hard requirement (real-time apps, gaming).
Some data loss is acceptable (media streaming).
High-volume telemetry or logs where the occasional loss doesn't matter.
You don't need browser support, or you already have an alternative channel for browsers.
tradeoff: 低延迟可丢包 vs 可靠交付需保序

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

optionExplanations: 延迟是硬指标时，UDP 省掉握手和重传等待，直接把延迟压到最低。
媒体流丢一帧只是轻微卡顿，能容忍丢失就没必要为完整性支付重传的延迟代价。
遥测/日志量大且偶尔丢几条不影响整体判断时，UDP 的低开销比逐条可靠投递更划算。
浏览器原生不支持裸 UDP，选它前要确认目标端不是普通浏览器，或已准备好替代通道。
optionExplanations_en: when latency is a hard requirement, UDP skips handshake and retransmission waits, keeping it lowest.
losing a media frame is a minor glitch, so tolerable loss removes any reason to pay retransmission latency.
with high-volume telemetry where a few dropped entries don't skew the picture, UDP's low overhead wins.
browsers lack a native raw-UDP API, so confirm the target isn't a plain browser or has a fallback channel.

scenario: 做浏览器视频会议：登录鉴权一次都不能错，音视频帧可以丢但必须低延迟。
scenario_en: You're building a browser video meeting product where login and auth can never fail, but media frames may drop as long as latency stays low.
q: 一个基于 Web 的视频会议应用，典型的协议组合是？
q_en: What protocol mix is typical for a web-based video meeting app?
options: TCP 管信令鉴权，UDP 传音视频
全部走 UDP，包括登录
全部走 TCP，包括视频帧
信令走 UDP 图省事，视频帧走 TCP
why: 现代应用经常混搭：控制面（信令、鉴权）要可靠所以走 TCP/HTTP；媒体面要低延迟、容忍丢帧所以走 UDP/WebRTC。
why_en: A web conferencing app typically uses TCP and HTTP for signaling and authentication but UDP via WebRTC for the audio and video streams.

flowchart LR C["客户端"] -->|HTTP/TCP
信令 鉴权| S["服务端"] C <-->|WebRTC/UDP

options_en: TCP handles signaling and auth, UDP carries the audio and video.
Everything over UDP, including login.
Everything over TCP, including video frames.
Signaling over UDP for simplicity, video frames over TCP.

optionExplanations: 登录、鉴权这些控制信息必须完整送达，走可靠的 TCP/HTTP；画面能丢帧换低延迟，走 UDP/WebRTC。
登录鉴权这类必须完整到达的数据不适合 UDP，丢包会直接导致登录失败或状态不一致。
视频帧全走 TCP 会让丢包变成重传排队，卡顿反而更严重，不符合实时媒体的取舍。
这把信令和视频该用的协议完全说反了——信令要可靠该用 TCP，视频要低延迟该用 UDP。
optionExplanations_en: the control plane (login, auth, signaling) needs TCP/HTTP; the media plane needs low-latency UDP/WebRTC.
login and auth data must arrive intact, so UDP isn't suitable — a dropped packet breaks login state.
sending every video frame over TCP turns loss into retransmission queuing, making glitches worse.
this swaps the two — signaling needs TCP's reliability, video needs UDP's low latency.

scenario: 你的 Web 服务要在高峰时从 10 台自动扩到 200 台，实例随时可能被杀掉重建。
scenario_en: Your web service has to autoscale from ten to two hundred instances at peak, with any instance killed and replaced at any moment.
q: 「HTTP 是无状态协议」意味着什么？为什么这是好事？
q_en: What does it mean that HTTP is stateless, and why is that useful?
options: 无状态意味着 HTTP 不能携带任何 cookie
每个请求彼此独立，服务器无需记住之前的请求
服务器不能存任何数据
请求之间必须间隔一秒
why: 无状态让服务器可以随意横向扩展、随意替换。系统设计的一般原则：能无状态就无状态，把有状态的表面积压到最小。
why_en: HTTP is stateless because each request is independent, which is good since you want to minimize the stateful surface area of your system.
options_en: Statelessness means HTTP cannot carry any cookies at all.
Each request is independent and the server doesn't need to remember prior requests.
The server cannot store any data.
Requests must be spaced at least a second apart.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

optionExplanations: 无状态跟能不能带 cookie 无关，cookie 只是客户端自己保存、随请求带上的数据。
无状态指每个请求都独立，服务器不用记住上一个请求的上下文，这才让服务器能随意扩展替换。
无状态是「协议不替你记会话」，服务器完全可以存数据，只是不能靠协议本身记住谁是谁。
HTTP 协议本身对请求间隔没有任何强制要求，这条限制根本不存在。
optionExplanations_en: statelessness has nothing to do with cookies — cookies are client-stored data sent with requests.
statelessness means each request stands alone with no remembered context, letting servers scale freely.
statelessness means the protocol itself doesn't track sessions; the server can still store data.
HTTP itself imposes no required gap between requests — that constraint doesn't exist.

scenario: 你在设计公开 API，网关会自动重试幂等（idempotent）的方法，方法语义必须选对。
scenario_en: You're designing a public API where the gateway auto-retries idempotent methods, so the method semantics have to be right.
q: 关于 HTTP 请求方法的约定，正确的是？
q_en: Which convention for HTTP methods is correct?
options: POST 按约定应该是幂等的
PUT 是用来删除资源的方法
PATCH 是用来整体替换整个资源的方法
GET 是 safe 且幂等的，通常不带请求体；DELETE 不是 safe，但也是幂等的
why: RFC 9110 区分 safe（只读，不改服务端状态）和 idempotent（重复多次的预期效果与一次相同）。GET 两者都是；它的请求体没有定义语义，可能被服务器或中间层拒绝，所以通常不带。DELETE 会改状态所以不 safe，但删一次和删十次结果相同，是幂等的，网关可以自动重试。POST 不保证幂等；PUT 是整体替换（或创建）；PATCH 是部分修改。
why_en: RFC 9110 separates safe (read-only, no server state change) from idempotent (repeating it has the same intended effect as once). GET is both; a GET body has no defined semantics and may be rejected, so it normally has none. DELETE changes state so it is not safe, but deleting once or ten times ends the same, so it is idempotent and a gateway may retry it. POST is not guaranteed idempotent; PUT replaces (or creates) a resource; PATCH applies a partial modification.
options_en: POST should conventionally be idempotent.
PUT is the method used to delete a resource.
PATCH is the method used to fully replace the entire resource.
GET is safe and idempotent and normally carries no body; DELETE is not safe but is idempotent too.
codeSample:
GET    /orders/42        HTTP/1.1   # 幂等，无 body，重复调用结果一致
POST   /orders           HTTP/1.1   # 创建新资源，不是幂等的
DELETE /orders/42        HTTP/1.1   # 幂等：删一次和删十次效果相同

optionExplanations: POST 按约定是非幂等的，重复提交会创建多个资源，这正是它和 PUT 的关键区别。
PUT 是整体更新（或创建）资源，删除资源对应的是 DELETE。
整体替换资源是 PUT 的职责，PATCH 按约定是部分更新。
GET 只读（safe），重复调用无副作用，请求体没有定义语义所以通常不带；DELETE 会改状态所以不 safe，但删一次和删十次结果相同，是幂等的。
optionExplanations_en: POST is conventionally non-idempotent — repeating it creates duplicates, unlike PUT.
PUT replaces (or creates) a resource wholesale; deleting one is DELETE's job.
replacing a resource wholesale is PUT's job; PATCH is conventionally a partial update.

GET is read-only (safe) with no side effect on repeat, and its body has no defined semantics so it normally has none; DELETE changes state so it is not safe, but deleting once or ten times ends the same, so it is idempotent.

q: 补全常见 HTTP 状态码：
q_en: Fill in the common HTTP status-code families.
text: {{200}} OK 成功；{{201}} Created 创建成功；301 永久移动；{{404}} Not Found 未找到；401 未认证；{{429}} Too Many Requests 触发限流；502 Bad Gateway 上游返回无效响应。
why: 2xx 成功、3xx 移动、4xx 客户端错、5xx 服务端错。429（限流）和 502（上游坏响应）在系统设计讨论里出镜率最高。
why_en: Two hundred means success, two-oh-one created, four-oh-four not found, four-twenty-nine rate limited, and five-oh-two a bad response from the upstream server.

scenario: 你要设计一个多年不破坏兼容的 API 头部，老客户端不认新压缩算法也不能挂。
scenario_en: You need an API header design that stays compatible for years, so old clients that don't know a new compression algorithm still keep working.
q: HTTP 的内容协商（如 Accept-Encoding）为什么被拿来当 API 设计的范例？
q_en: Why is HTTP content negotiation, such as Accept-Encoding, a useful API design example?
options: 因为它强制所有客户端必须统一用 gzip
客户端声明能处理的编码，服务器选优编码返回
因为它是唯一的 HTTP 头
因为它能加密数据
why: 头部是灵活的键值对，Accept-Encoding 展示了如何设计对未知未来用例友好的接口：能力协商、向后兼容、优雅降级——HTTP 规范务实哲学的缩影。
why_en: Content negotiation lets clients advertise supported encodings so servers respond with the most efficient one, giving both backward compatibility and graceful degradation.
options_en: Because it forces every client to standardize on gzip.
The client declares which encodings it supports, and the server returns its best pick.
Because it's the only HTTP header that exists.
Because it encrypts the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 响应头，标明服务器实际用了哪种压缩编码（如 gzip）返回内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Content-Encoding is the HTTP response header stating which compression, like gzip, the server actually used for the body.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

optionExplanations: 它不强制任何编码——只是客户端表达自己支持哪些，服务器完全可以选择不压缩。
客户端在头里声明自己能处理哪些编码，服务器从中选一个最优返回——这是能力协商、向后兼容的范例。
HTTP 头有几十个（Content-Type、Authorization 等）；这只是其中一个，不是唯一存在的头。
编码协商跟加密无关：加密是 TLS/HTTPS 的职责，这个头只管压缩格式的协商。
optionExplanations_en: Accept-Encoding doesn't force any encoding — the client just states support, server can pick none.
the client declares supported encodings and the server picks the best match — capability negotiation.
HTTP has dozens of headers (Content-Type, Authorization); Accept-Encoding is just one of them.
encoding negotiation is unrelated to encryption; that's TLS/HTTPS's job, not Accept-Encoding's.

scenario: 你的登录接口在公共 WiFi 上被抓包，密码明文可见，要在协议层把这个洞堵上。
scenario_en: Your login endpoint got sniffed on public WiFi with the password visible in plaintext, and you need a protocol-level fix.
q: HTTPS 在 HTTP 之上加了什么？
q_en: What does HTTPS add on top of HTTP?
options: TLS/SSL 安全层：加密防窃听
一层负责压缩响应体积、省带宽的压缩层
一层缓存热点数据的缓存层
一层做请求分发的负载均衡层
why: HTTPS = HTTP + TLS/SSL，请求响应内容在传输中被加密。做公开网站，用 HTTPS 没有商量余地。
why_en: HTTPS adds a TLS security layer that encrypts communications against eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks, and public websites use it without exception.
options_en: A TLS/SSL security layer that encrypts against eavesdropping.
A compression layer that shrinks the response body and saves bandwidth.
A caching layer that stores hot data.
A load-balancing layer that spreads requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 HTTP 之上加一层 TLS/SSL 加密，防窃听和中间人攻击。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTPS layers TLS/SSL encryption on top of HTTP to prevent eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.

termDefinitions.fullName: Transport Layer Security / Secure Sockets Layer
termDefinitions.meaning: 给网络连接加密和身份验证的协议，SSL 是 TLS 的前身。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TLS, the successor to SSL, encrypts and authenticates a network connection.

optionExplanations: HTTPS 就是在 HTTP 基础上加一层 TLS/SSL，把传输内容加密，防止被中间人窃听或篡改。

load balancing is a separate architectural component, unrelated to HTTP encryption.

scenario: 转账 API 全站已上 HTTPS，但请求体里带的 userId 依然能被客户端随意改。
scenario_en: Your transfer API is fully on HTTPS, yet the userId carried in the request body can still be freely tampered with by the client.
q: 这个场景暴露的是哪一类安全错误？
q_en: Which security mistake does this scenario expose?
options: 忘记按时续期证书，导致证书过期失效
用了太旧、早已被淘汰的 TLS 协议版本
把用户密码明文直接写进了请求 URL 参数里
信任请求体内容，如直接用 user ID 查库
why: HTTPS 只保护传输中不被偷看和篡改，不保证请求体内容是可信的。服务端用请求体里的 userId 直接查库/扣款，攻击者改个数字就能操作别人的账户；身份应来自服务端验证过的会话或 token。其他选项是真实问题，但不是这个场景描述的那一个。
why_en: HTTPS protects data in transit, not the trustworthiness of the body. Using the body's userId directly lets an attacker act on another account; identity must come from a server-verified session or token. The other options are real issues, but not the one this scenario describes.
options_en: Forgetting to renew the certificate on time, so it lapses.
Using an outdated TLS version that was deprecated long ago.
Putting a user's password in plaintext right inside the request URL.
Trusting the request body's contents, like using a raw user id to query the database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 HTTP 之上加一层 TLS/SSL 加密，防窃听和中间人攻击。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTPS layers TLS/SSL encryption on top of HTTP to prevent eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.

optionExplanations: 证书过期确实是常见运维事故，但它不是「加密了传输却仍不安全」这条思路要指的错误。
旧版 TLS 是配置层面的疏漏，跟这里说的「加密内容却还有安全漏洞」不是同一类问题。
把密码写进 URL 确实是坏习惯，但 HTTPS 下它同样被加密，风险在于 URL 会被日志、浏览器历史留存，属于另一类问题。
HTTPS 只保证传输不被偷看，不保证请求体真的来自可信客户端；直接信任 user ID 查库，攻击者照样能伪造。
optionExplanations_en: Certificate expiry is a real ops failure, but not the mistake that survives even with encryption turned on.
An outdated TLS version is a config gap, a different category from the mistake described here.
Putting a password in the URL is a bad habit, but HTTPS still encrypts it — the risk is URLs landing in logs and history, a different category.
HTTPS only protects transit, not whether the body is genuinely trusted — trusting a user ID lets it be forged.

REST: simple, flexible, a universal baseline.
gRPC.
A custom binary protocol built for peak performance.

rows: 默认，通用 Web/服务 API
内部高性能服务间通信

The exact ratio depends on value lengths: the longer the values, the smaller the gap.

scenario_en: In a microservice architecture, internal calls are high-volume and performance-sensitive, while you also expose a public API to external users.
q: 推荐的组合是？
q_en: What protocol combination is recommended for this microservice architecture?
options: 内部服务间用 gRPC，对外公开 API 用 REST
不管内外，统统强行都上 gRPC
内部服务间用 REST，对外公开 API 用 gRPC
无论内外，全部统一都用 WebSocket
why: gRPC 是二进制协议、工具链对外部用户不友好，所以公开 API 用 REST；内部服务间用 gRPC 拿性能。面试里内外都 REST 也完全可以，按需演进。
why_en: Use gRPC for internal service-to-service communication where performance matters and REST for public-facing APIs whose clients you do not control.
whenOtherWins: 如果内部调用瓶颈在服务器计算而非网络、或团队工具链不熟，内外统一 REST 更简单，之后按需演进。
options_en: gRPC for internal service-to-service calls, REST for the public API.
Force gRPC everywhere regardless, both internal and external.
REST for internal service-to-service calls, gRPC for the public API.
WebSocket for absolutely everything, inside and out.
tradeoff: gRPC 内部高性能 vs REST 外部通用

rows: 二进制更快，团队可控工具链
JSON 通用，客户端工具链成熟

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 发起的高性能 RPC 框架，基于 HTTP/2 和 Protocol Buffers 二进制序列化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is Google's high-performance RPC framework built on HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers binary serialization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把系统建模成「资源」、用标准 HTTP 方法操作它们的 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that models a system as resources manipulated with standard HTTP verbs.

optionExplanations: 内部通信量大、性能关键时用 gRPC 换性能；对外面向不受控客户端，用 REST 保持通用兼容。
对外也上 gRPC 会让外部开发者被迫接入二进制协议和陌生工具链，除非所有调用方都受你控制。
这把内外该用的协议说反了——外部公开场景需要 REST 的通用性，内部高性能场景才是 gRPC 的主场。
WebSocket 是为持久双向通信设计的，用来承载普通的请求-响应式服务调用属于用错工具。
optionExplanations_en: use gRPC internally for high-traffic, performance-critical calls, and REST externally for broad compatibility.
Forcing gRPC externally makes outsiders adopt a binary protocol — unfriendly unless you control every caller.
This flips which side needs which protocol — the public surface needs REST, gRPC's home is the internal path.
WebSocket is built for persistent two-way traffic; using it for plain request-response is the wrong tool.

q: RPC 和 gRPC 是什么关系?
q_en: How are RPC and gRPC related?
options: RPC 是「远程调用像本地调用」的概念;gRPC 是它的一个具体框架(HTTP/2 + protobuf + 代码生成 + 4 种调用类型)
gRPC 是概念,RPC 是 Google 出的具体框架
两者是竞争关系,gRPC 用来取代 RPC 这个协议
RPC 只能传 JSON,gRPC 只能传 XML
options_en: RPC is the concept of calling a remote function like a local one; gRPC is one concrete framework for it (HTTP/2 + protobuf + code generation + four call types)
gRPC is the concept and RPC is Google's concrete framework
They compete, and gRPC is meant to replace an RPC protocol
RPC can only carry JSON and gRPC can only carry XML
why: RPC 是「远程函数像本地函数一样调用」这个概念；gRPC 是 Google 的一种具体实现，选了 HTTP/2、protobuf、代码生成和四种调用类型。
why_en: RPC is the remote-call concept, while gRPC is Google's concrete RPC framework built on HTTP/2, protobuf, code generation, and four call shapes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种编程概念:调用远程机器上的函数就像调用本地函数一样,底层帮你打包请求、走网络、取回结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPC (Remote Procedure Call) is the concept of invoking a function on a remote machine as if it were local, with the framework packing the request, crossing the network, and returning the result.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 做的具体 RPC 框架:HTTP/2 传输 + protobuf 序列化 + .proto 代码生成 + 四种调用类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is Google's concrete RPC framework: HTTP/2 transport, protobuf serialization, code generation from .proto, and four call types.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP/2 是 HTTP 的二进制多路复用版本，gRPC 用它承载高效的双向流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/2 is the binary, multiplexed version of HTTP that gRPC uses for efficient bidirectional streams.

termDefinitions.meaning: gRPC 用的接口定义语言与二进制序列化格式,带 schema、编码比 JSON 小很多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Protocol Buffers is gRPC's interface definition language and binary serialization format — schema-typed and much smaller than JSON.

termDefinitions.fullName: JavaScript Object Notation Remote Procedure Call
termDefinitions.meaning: JSON-RPC 是用 JSON 编码请求和响应的一种 RPC 实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSON-RPC is an RPC implementation that encodes requests and responses as JSON.

termDefinitions.meaning: XML 是一种文本标记格式，不是 gRPC 使用的序列化格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XML is a text markup format, not the serialization format used by gRPC.

optionExplanations: 对:这条把抽象层级放对了,并点出 gRPC 自己绑定的传输、编码和代码生成选择。
说反了:RPC 才是概念,gRPC 是具体实现。
gRPC 不是「取代 RPC」,它本身就是 RPC 的一种实现——概念和实现不是竞争关系。
编码格式说错了:RPC 是概念不绑定格式,gRPC 用的是 protobuf(不是 XML)。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: RPC is the concept; gRPC is one framework with HTTP/2, protobuf, code generation, and four call shapes.
Reversed: RPC is the concept and gRPC is a concrete implementation.
gRPC does not 'replace RPC' — it is itself an RPC implementation; a concept and its implementation do not compete.
Wrong on encoding: RPC as a concept is format-agnostic, and gRPC uses protobuf, not XML.

q: gRPC 的 server streaming(一次调用返回一串)和「异步卸载」(秒回 job_id、后台处理)有什么区别?
q_en: How does gRPC server streaming (one call returns a stream) differ from async offload (return a job_id immediately, process in the background)?
options: streaming 是一条调用【一直开着】、结果陆续流回;异步卸载是【秒回 ticket、调用即结束】,结果从另开的通道送
两者完全一样,都叫异步,没有区别
server streaming 会立刻返回 job_id,然后靠 webhook 把结果送回来
异步卸载必须保持同一条连接一直开着,直到结果返回才断开
options_en: Streaming keeps one call open with results trickling back; async offload returns a ticket immediately, ends the call, and delivers results over a separate channel
They are exactly the same — both are just 'async' with no difference
Server streaming returns a job_id immediately and then delivers results via webhook
Async offload must keep the same connection open until the result returns
why: Server streaming 是同一条调用保持打开，服务端按序推回多条结果；异步卸载是立刻回 job_id 并结束调用，后台 worker 之后从轮询/SSE/webhook 等另一路径给结果。
why_en: Server streaming keeps one call open for a stream of results, while async offload returns a job_id immediately and delivers the result later through another channel.
whenOtherWins: 中间结果要边到边显示就选 streaming；任务很久且客户端可先走，就选异步卸载。
tradeoff: streaming 的「实时边到边、但占住一条连接」 vs 异步卸载的「秒回不占连接、但结果要另开通道且有延迟」

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求,服务端在同一个调用/连接上按序陆续推回一串响应,连接全程保持。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Server streaming: one request, and the server pushes a sequence of responses back on the same call/connection, which stays open throughout.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求立刻返回一个 job_id 并结束,真正的处理交给后台 worker,结果之后从另一条通道送回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Async offload returns a job_id immediately and ends the request, hands the work to a background worker, and delivers the result later over a separate channel.

optionExplanations: 对:一个保留调用推多条结果,一个先发 ticket 后台处理后另路通知。
混成「都是异步」会漏掉连接是否被占住、结果是否同路返回这两个差异。
job_id 加 webhook 是异步卸载的形状,不是 server streaming。
一直等在同一条连接上是 streaming,异步卸载的重点是不占住连接。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: one keeps the call open for many results; the other returns a ticket and reports later elsewhere.
Calling both async hides the key difference: whether the same connection stays occupied.
A job_id plus webhook is async offload, not server streaming.
Holding one connection until results arrive is streaming; offload returns without holding it.

scenario: 系统设计面试只剩 35 分钟，核心数据模型还没画，你却想争论 REST 还是 gRPC。
scenario_en: Thirty-five minutes are left in the system design interview, the core data model isn't drawn yet, and you're about to argue REST versus gRPC.
q: 这时死磕 RPC 协议选择为什么是错的？面试官真正在看什么？
q_en: Why is over-focusing on RPC protocol choice a mistake here — what is the interviewer actually evaluating?
options: 协议选择永远是面试的重点
面试就是要画出最优架构图
面试官考察的是你如何思考问题、应对新约束
REST 已经够好、永远都不需要任何优化
why: 面试不是在白板上抠最优解，而是展示思考过程。先解决实质性瓶颈，协议微调放最后——除非面试官主动把你往那里带。
why_en: Interviewers want to see how you think through problems, so beware of hyperoptimizing your RPC protocol choice before handling the substantial bottlenecks.
options_en: Protocol choice is always the top priority in an interview.
The interview is about drawing the single optimal architecture on the whiteboard.
Interviewers care about how you think through a problem and react to new constraints.
REST is already good enough and never needs any optimization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让程序像调用本地函数一样调用远程服务上的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPC lets a program invoke a method on a remote service as if it were a local function call.

optionExplanations: 协议选择只是很小的一环，面试官更在意你怎么权衡取舍，而不是死磕某个协议名字。
面试考察的是思考过程而不是画出一张「标准答案」架构图，过程比结果更重要。
面试官真正想看的是你怎么发现约束、怎么权衡取舍、遇到新信息怎么调整方案。
REST 在超高吞吐场景确实有短板，但优化协议不该是面试早期就死磕的重点。
optionExplanations_en: protocol choice is a small piece — interviewers care about weighing tradeoffs, not the right name.
interviews assess process, not a single 'model answer' diagram — process matters more than the artifact.
interviewers want to see how you surface constraints, weigh tradeoffs, and adjust as new info arrives.
REST does have shortfalls at extreme throughput, but that shouldn't be an early-interview fixation.

scenario: AI 聊天产品要把生成中的 token 边生成边推给浏览器，用户不能等整段回复。
scenario_en: An AI chat product has to push tokens to the browser as they are generated, because users can't wait for the whole reply.
q: Server-Sent Events（SSE）的本质是什么？
q_en: What is Server-Sent Events, or SSE, at its core?
options: 一种新的传输层协议
客户端向服务器的推送通道
WebSocket 协议早期的另一个旧称
HTTP 上的推送妙招：单响应多消息
why: 普通 HTTP 要等整个响应收完才能处理；SSE 让一个 text/event-stream 响应变成消息流：服务器持续写出事件，每个事件由若干 data: 行组成、以空行结束，浏览器 EventSource 每收到一个完整事件就触发一次。
why_en: Plain HTTP processes a response only once it is complete; SSE turns one text/event-stream response into a message stream: each event is one or more data: lines terminated by a blank line, and EventSource fires once per complete event.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Browser
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: HTTP request
    S-->>C: chunk 1
    S-->>C: chunk 2
    S-->>C: chunk 3
    Note over C,S: 单向事件流
options_en: A brand-new transport-layer protocol.
A push channel from client to server.
An earlier alternate name for the WebSocket protocol.
A push trick on HTTP: many messages in one response.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP 的单向推送标准，服务器在一个长响应里持续发送多条消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE is an HTTP-based standard for one-way server push that streams multiple messages over a single long response.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的文本序列化格式，键值对结构、人类可读但比二进制格式占空间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSON is a common text-based serialization format that is human-readable but bulkier than binary formats.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

optionExplanations: SSE 不是新的传输层协议，它建立在普通 HTTP 之上，走的还是 TCP。
SSE 的推送方向是服务器到客户端（单向），不是客户端向服务器推。
SSE 和 WebSocket 是两种不同的技术，各有独立协议和用法，不是同一个东西改了名字。
SSE 把多条消息放进一个长响应里，每个以空行结束的事件是一条消息，由 EventSource 逐个触发。
optionExplanations_en: SSE isn't a new transport protocol — it's built on plain HTTP and still rides over TCP.
SSE pushes server-to-client only (one direction), not the client pushing to the server.
SSE and WebSocket are distinct technologies with their own protocols, not a renamed same thing.
SSE packs many messages into one long HTTP response — each event, ended by a blank line, is one message that EventSource fires in turn.

scenario: 股价推送流用 SSE，服务器给每条报价设置了 id，并在内存里保留最近 1 分钟的报价。流被中间代理掐断 3 秒，客户端重连后不能漏掉这期间的报价。
scenario_en: A stock price stream uses SSE; the server tags each quote with an id and keeps the last minute of quotes in memory. A proxy cuts the stream for three seconds, and after reconnecting the client must not miss the quotes from that gap.
q: SSE 连接被关闭后（服务器/负载均衡器/中间代理都可能关它），标准提供的客户端恢复机制是？
q_en: After an SSE connection closes, what recovery mechanism does the standard give the client?
options: 客户端必须靠用户手动刷新页面
带 last ID 自动重连
所有消息从头重发
连接永远不会被关闭
why: 标准规定 EventSource 断线后自动重连，并在重连请求头里带 Last-Event-ID（最后收到的事件 id）。补发错过的报价是服务器自己的职责：它要保留近期事件并按这个 id 续传——题面里的 1 分钟缓冲正是为此准备。
why_en: The standard makes EventSource reconnect automatically and send a Last-Event-ID header with the last received event id. Resending missed quotes is the server's own job: it must retain recent events and resume from that id, which is what the one-minute buffer is for.
options_en: The client relies on the user manually refreshing the page.
It auto-reconnects with the last message id.
Every message is resent from the very beginning.
The connection is never closed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP 的单向推送标准，服务器在一个长响应里持续发送多条消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE is an HTTP-based standard for one-way server push that streams multiple messages over a single long response.

optionExplanations: SSE 标准里的 EventSource 会自动重连，不需要用户手动刷新页面。
EventSource 断线后自动重连，并在请求头带上最后收到的事件 id（Last-Event-ID）；按它补发错过的消息是服务器自己的实现，标准不强制。
不是从头重发全部历史，而是从客户端记住的 last ID 之后补发，服务器要负责保留这段历史。
SSE 连接会被服务器、负载均衡器或中间代理主动关闭，这正是标准要定义重连机制的原因。
optionExplanations_en: SSE's EventSource reconnects automatically — the user doesn't need to manually refresh.
EventSource reconnects on its own and sends the last received event id as Last-Event-ID; resending what was missed is the server's own implementation, not mandated by the standard.
it isn't a full history replay — the server resends only from the remembered last ID onward.
SSE connections do get closed by the server, LB, or a proxy — hence the standard's reconnect rule.

scenario: SSE 推送在本地一切正常，上线经过公司代理后前端却一次性收到全部消息。
scenario_en: SSE streaming works fine locally, but in production behind the corporate proxy the frontend receives all the messages at once.
q: 实践中 SSE（Server-Sent Events）有什么「隐坑」？
q_en: What hidden operational issue does SSE often have in practice?
options: 浏览器不支持 SSE
SSE 无法传 JSON
代理会把 SSE 缓冲成一次性响应
SSE 一条连接最多只能发 10 条消息
why: 多数面试官不了解这些限制，但了解它们能证明你真用过 SSE：连接会被中间设备掐断、某些网络会把流缓冲成一坨。真实世界满是取舍。
why_en: Some misbehaving networks batch all SSE chunks into a single response, defeating the streaming behavior, a pain anyone who has shipped SSE knows well.
options_en: Browsers don't support SSE.
SSE can't carry JSON.
A proxy can buffer all the SSE chunks into one response.
A single SSE connection can send at most 10 messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP 的单向推送标准，服务器在一个长响应里持续发送多条消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE is an HTTP-based standard for one-way server push that streams multiple messages over a single long response.

optionExplanations: 主流浏览器原生支持 SSE 的 EventSource API，这不是它的坑。
SSE 的 data 字段可以放任意文本，JSON 序列化后一样能传，不受限制。
某些中间代理会把流式响应整体缓冲起来，直到攒够一批或结束才一次性吐出，破坏了 SSE 想要的实时性。
SSE 对消息条数没有协议层限制，只要连接不断就能一直发。
optionExplanations_en: mainstream browsers natively support SSE's EventSource API, so that isn't the gotcha.
SSE's data field carries any text, and serialized JSON fits fine — there's no such restriction.
some proxies buffer the whole streaming response and flush it all at once, defeating SSE's real-time point.
SSE has no protocol-level cap on message count — it sends as long as the connection stays open.

scenario: 在线拍卖系统：要让竞拍者实时看到当前最高出价——服务器到客户端的单向推送，客户端不需要高频回传。
scenario_en: In an online auction, bidders need to see the current highest bid in real time; the server pushes updates one way, and clients rarely send back data.
q: 最合适的实时方案是？
q_en: What is the best real-time delivery option for this online auction?
options: SSE：单向推送，比 WebSocket 轻
上全双工双向长连接的 WebSocket，功能更全
每隔 30 秒轮询一次
点对点直连的 WebRTC
why: 「事件一发生客户端就要知道，但只是单向通知」是 SSE 的标准适用场景——拍卖出价、通知流都是。不需要为单向推送付 WebSocket 的基建成本。
why_en: SSE is the right fit for pushing auction price updates because the flow is server-to-client only and WebSockets would be overkill.
whenOtherWins: 需要高频双向通信（聊天打字、多人游戏操作）时才升级到 WebSocket。
options_en: SSE: one-way push, much lighter than WebSocket.
A full-duplex, bidirectional, persistent WebSocket with more capability.
Polling once every 30 seconds.
Direct peer-to-peer over WebRTC.
tradeoff: SSE 单向轻量 vs WebSocket 双向重基建

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP 的单向推送标准，服务器在一个长响应里持续发送多条消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE is an HTTP-based standard for one-way server push that streams multiple messages over a single long response.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上提供持久、双向通信的协议，通过 HTTP upgrade 建立。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that provides a persistent, bidirectional channel over one TCP connection, established via an HTTP upgrade.

optionExplanations: 只需要服务器往客户端单向推送出价更新，SSE 用更轻量的基建就能满足，不用多付双向通信的代价。
WebSocket 提供全双工双向通信，但客户端不需要高频回传，为单向需求上双向长连接基建是过度设计。
轮询有固定间隔，出价发生和客户端看到之间会有延迟，跟「实时看到最高出价」的要求不匹配。
WebRTC 是为点对点直连设计的（如音视频通话），拍卖场景是服务器广播给多个竞拍者，不是两端直连。
optionExplanations_en: with only server-to-client push needed for bids, SSE meets it with lighter infrastructure than two-way.
WebSocket gives full-duplex traffic, but this client never sends back at high frequency — over-engineering.
Polling has a fixed interval, so there's a lag between a bid happening and the client seeing it.
WebRTC is built for direct peer links; an auction is one server broadcasting to many bidders, not two peers.

scenario: 在线协作白板：任一用户的笔画要在 100ms 内出现在其他人屏幕上，两端都要推。
scenario_en: On a collaborative whiteboard, any user's stroke has to appear on everyone else's screen within a hundred milliseconds, pushing in both directions.
q: WebSocket 提供什么能力？
q_en: What capability does WebSocket provide?
options: 只能服务器向客户端推送
无状态的请求-响应
持久连接上的双向实时通信
点对点直连
why: 与 HTTP 请求-响应模型不同，WebSocket 是持久双向通道：双方都能不经对方请求就发消息，浏览器支持好——这是它对 gRPC 流式的关键优势。
why_en: WebSockets provide a persistent bidirectional connection with broad browser support, letting the server push data without waiting for a request.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: message
    S-->>C: push
    C->>S: message
    S-->>C: push
    Note over C,S: 一条持久双向连接
options_en: It can only push from server to client.
It's stateless request-response.
Real-time bidirectional communication over a persistent connection.

scenario_en: Internal service-to-service calls run at a million per second, and every extra hop through a central load balancer adds latency and a single point of failure.
q: 客户端负载均衡是怎么工作的？优势是什么？
q_en: How does client-side load balancing work, and what is its advantage?
options: 客户端把每个请求都发给中心代理，由它转发
服务器靠随机拒绝请求来实现负载均衡
全部由 DNS 服务器负责处理所有路由决策
客户端从服务注册中心拿服务器列表、自己决定连谁
why: 客户端自己做决策：先向注册中心/目录要可用服务器列表，然后直连目标。快且高效——不用每个请求都过一遍负载均衡器，只要定期（或被推送）更新列表。
why_en: In client-side load balancing the client fetches the server list from a registry and picks a server itself, avoiding an extra network hop on every request.
options_en: The client sends every request to a central proxy that forwards them.
The server balances load by randomly rejecting some requests.
The DNS server alone handles every single routing decision.
The client fetches the server list from a service registry and decides itself which one to call.
tradeoff: 客户端自决省一跳 vs 依赖注册中心同步及时性

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录当前有哪些可用服务器实例及其地址的目录服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service registry is the directory service that tracks which server instances are currently available and where they are.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器、并监控它们健康状态的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer is the component that distributes requests across multiple backend servers and monitors their health.

optionExplanations: 把请求发给中心代理转发正是「服务端负载均衡」的做法，跟客户端负载均衡的定义相反。
随机拒绝请求不是负载均衡的实现方式，那只会制造无谓的失败。
DNS 只是客户端负载均衡里的一种实现手段（轮转 IP），不是「处理所有路由」的中心角色。
客户端先向注册中心要一份可用服务器列表，再自己挑一台直连，省掉了过一遍中心 LB 的那一跳。
optionExplanations_en: sending requests to a central proxy is server-side load balancing, the opposite of client-side.
randomly rejecting requests isn't a load-balancing technique — it just creates needless failures.
DNS is one implementation of client-side balancing (rotating IPs), not a central routing role.
the client asks a registry for a server list, then connects directly, skipping the hop through a central LB.

rows: 靠列表刷新周期，有延迟
LB 主动健康检查，更快

scenario: Redis 集群把数据分到 16384 个槽，客户端要在一次网络往返内命中正确的分片节点。
scenario_en: A Redis cluster spreads data across 16384 slots, and the client has to hit the right shard node within a single round trip.
q: Redis Cluster 是客户端负载均衡的好例子，它如何运作？
q_en: How does Redis Cluster demonstrate client-side load balancing?
options: 哈希 key 直连，错了收到 MOVED
靠一个中央路由代理服务器统一分发所有请求
客户端每次随机连一个节点碰运气
用 DNS 轮转决定分片
why: Redis Cluster：gossip 让每个节点掌握全集群拓扑；客户端先问任一节点拿到节点+分片信息，之后 hash key → 定分片 → 直连；发错了节点会回 MOVED 告诉你去哪。
why_en: Redis Cluster nodes gossip cluster state, clients hash the key to pick the shard and connect directly, and a wrong node helpfully replies with MOVED.
options_en: It hashes the key to connect directly, getting MOVED if wrong.
A central routing proxy server uniformly dispatches every request.
The client connects to a random node and hopes for the best.
DNS round robin decides the shard.
codeSample:
> GET user:1000:profile
(error) MOVED 3999 127.0.0.1:6381
# 客户端按提示重连 6381 端口，并把这个 slot 的归属缓存在本地

termDefinitions.meaning: 节点间两两随机交换状态信息、让全网逐渐收敛到一致视图的通信方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A gossip protocol lets nodes randomly exchange state with each other until the whole cluster converges on a consistent view.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Cluster 返回的重定向响应，告诉客户端目标 key 实际在哪个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MOVED is the redirect response Redis Cluster returns to tell the client which node actually owns a key.

optionExplanations: 客户端对 key 做哈希算出该去哪个分片，直接连对应节点；连错了会收到 MOVED，告诉它去哪重试。
Redis Cluster 没有中央路由服务器，节点靠 gossip 协议互相同步拓扑，客户端直连节点。
随机连节点大概率连错分片，Redis Cluster 靠哈希槽而不是运气来定位数据。
分片是靠哈希槽（hash slot）分配决定的，跟 DNS 轮转毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: the client hashes the key to find its shard and connects directly; a wrong guess gets a MOVED redirect.
Redis Cluster has no central router — nodes sync topology via gossip, clients connect directly.
randomly picking a node likely hits the wrong shard; Cluster locates data via hash slots, not luck.
shard assignment comes from hash slots, unrelated to DNS round-robin.

scenario: 你有两台负载均衡器，但域名目前只解析到其中一台的 IP，它挂了整个服务就不可用；你不想再加一层设备来给它们分流。
scenario_en: You have two load balancers, but the domain currently resolves only to one of them, so if it fails the whole service is down; you don't want yet another device in front of them.
q: DNS 如何充当「客户端负载均衡器」？这还顺带解决了什么经典问题？
q_en: How can DNS act as a client-side load balancer, and what classic problem does that help solve?
options: DNS 会实时检测每台服务器的负载并智能路由
DNS 会主动把请求转发给当前最空闲的那台服务器
DNS 返回两台 LB 的 IP 并轮转顺序分散流量；配合健康检查摘除挂掉的那台，去掉对单台 LB 的依赖
DNS 会把所有的响应内容都缓存下来
why: DNS 每次解析返回轮转顺序的 IP 列表，客户端自然分散到两台 LB。要真正容错，还需要 DNS 健康检查把挂掉的 LB 记录摘掉；恢复速度受 TTL 缓存限制，部分客户端也会自己重试列表里的下一个 IP。
why_en: DNS returns the IP list in rotating order so clients spread across both LBs. Real failover also needs DNS health checks to withdraw a dead LB; recovery is bounded by TTL caching, and some clients retry the next IP on their own.
options_en: DNS detects each server's real-time load and intelligently routes to it.
DNS actively forwards the request to whichever server is currently least busy.
DNS returns both LB IPs in rotating order to spread traffic and, with health checks removing a dead one, removes dependence on a single LB
DNS caches every single response it ever returns.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的分布式查找系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器、并监控它们健康状态的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer is the component that distributes requests across multiple backend servers and monitors their health.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目或 DNS 记录被视为有效的最长时间，过期后必须刷新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the maximum time a cached value or DNS record is considered valid before it must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: 普通 DNS 不检测服务器实时负载，它只是按配置轮转返回的 IP 顺序或集合。
DNS 不转发请求，它只做名字到 IP 的解析，请求本身是客户端自己发出去的。
DNS 每次解析返回不同顺序的 IP，客户端自然分散；再配合 DNS 健康检查摘掉挂掉的 LB，就不再依赖单台 LB（受 TTL 缓存影响，不是瞬时）。
DNS 缓存跟这里说的「轮转分散流量」是两码事，缓存行为由 TTL 控制，不是「缓存所有响应」。
optionExplanations_en: plain DNS doesn't monitor real-time load — it rotates the order or set of IPs per configuration.
DNS doesn't forward requests — it only resolves names to IPs; the client sends the actual request.
Each lookup returns IPs in a different order, spreading clients; with DNS health checks withdrawing a dead LB you no longer depend on a single LB (bounded by TTL caching, not instant).
DNS caching is separate from 'rotate to spread traffic' — caching is governed by TTL, not this.

scenario: 判断客户端负载均衡适不适合你的系统。
scenario_en: You need to decide whether client-side load balancing fits your system.
q: 它在哪两类场景下工作得好？
q_en: In what two situations does client-side load balancing work well?
options: 任何只要存在负载均衡需求的场景都一律适用
少量受控客户端，或能容忍慢更新的大量客户端
只适合纯粹的单体应用架构
只适合纯移动端的应用场景
why: 受控的少量客户端推送更新很容易；海量客户端时更新耗时随客户端数增长，只能靠 TTL 类机制容忍慢更新。面试里内部微服务间用客户端 LB 表现非常好（gRPC 内置）。
why_en: Client-side load balancing works with a small number of controlled clients like internal gRPC services, or many clients that tolerate slow updates like DNS.
whenOtherWins: 大量不受控客户端 + 需要快速感知服务器变化 → 用专用（服务端）负载均衡器。
options_en: Any scenario with a load-balancing need whatsoever always applies.
A small controlled set of clients, or many clients that can tolerate slow updates.
Only purely monolithic application architectures.
Only purely mobile-only application scenarios.
tradeoff: 少量受控客户端自决 vs 大量客户端靠 TTL 容忍慢更新

rows: 少量受控 或 海量能忍慢

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service registry is the directory service that tracks which server instances are currently available and where they are.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器、并监控它们健康状态的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer is the component that distributes requests across multiple backend servers and monitors their health.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的分布式查找系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目或 DNS 记录被视为有效的最长时间，过期后必须刷新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the maximum time a cached value or DNS record is considered valid before it must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: 客户端负载均衡不是万能默认——客户端数量大且需要快速感知变化时，靠客户端自己维护列表反而不可靠。
客户端数量少而受控时推送更新很容易；数量大但能接受慢更新（靠 TTL 容忍）时也行得通——这是它的适用场景。
客户端负载均衡跟应用是不是单体没有关系，它描述的是「谁来决定连哪台服务器」，微服务里同样常见。
客户端负载均衡不限于移动端，内部微服务间调用（如 gRPC 内置）是它更典型的场景。
optionExplanations_en: Client-side balancing isn't universal — many clients needing fast updates makes self-kept lists unreliable.
few controlled clients make pushing updates easy; many clients tolerating slow (TTL-based) updates also work.
Client-side balancing has nothing to do with monolith versus microservice — it's about who picks the server.
Client-side balancing isn't mobile-only — internal service calls, built into gRPC, are the typical case.

scenario: 一台后端宕机要立刻摘掉，但它的 IP 早已通过 DNS 分发给了全球客户端。
scenario_en: A backend dies and has to be pulled right away, but its IP was already handed out to clients worldwide through DNS.
q: DNS 的 TTL 机制给「更新服务器列表」带来什么硬约束？
q_en: What hard constraint does DNS TTL create when updating server lists?
options: 各地 resolver 会在 TTL 内继续返回已缓存的旧记录，所以 DNS 改动无法立即生效；部分客户端缓存或已建立的连接甚至会拖得更久
TTL 越长，更新反而传播得越快
TTL 完全不影响更新速度
TTL 只会对走 HTTPS 的加密流量产生影响，对其他无效
why: TTL 允许各地 resolver 缓存解析结果（扩展性好），代价是摘掉一台坏服务器时，合规的缓存要等到 TTL 过期才会重新解析；TTL 是缓存上限而不是“全体客户端生效”的保证——不守 TTL 的客户端缓存和已经建立的长连接会让旧 IP 被用得更久。所以秒级摘除要靠 LB / health check，而不是只改 DNS。
why_en: TTL lets resolvers everywhere cache answers (good for scale), but it means that after you remove a bad server, compliant caches keep the old record until the TTL expires. TTL is a cache upper bound, not a guarantee that every client switches by then — client caches that ignore TTL and already-open connections can keep using the old IP longer. Fast removal therefore needs an LB / health checks, not just a DNS change.
options_en: Resolvers keep serving the cached old record until its TTL expires, so a DNS change can't take effect immediately — and some client-side caches or already-open connections can lag even longer.
A longer TTL makes updates propagate even faster.
TTL has no effect on update speed at all.
TTL only affects encrypted HTTPS traffic and nothing else.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的分布式查找系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目或 DNS 记录被视为有效的最长时间，过期后必须刷新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the maximum time a cached value or DNS record is considered valid before it must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: TTL 决定合规 resolver 缓存解析结果的时长，所以摘掉坏节点后旧记录会继续被返回到 TTL 过期；不守 TTL 的客户端缓存和已建立的长连接还会拖得更久。
TTL 越长意味着缓存越久不刷新，更新反而传播得更慢，不是更快。
TTL 直接决定了缓存过期前客户端看到的还是旧记录，对更新速度影响很大。
TTL 是 DNS 解析记录的缓存时间，跟走不走 HTTPS 完全无关，任何基于该记录的流量都受它影响。
optionExplanations_en: TTL sets how long compliant resolvers cache a result, so the old record keeps being served until the TTL expires after you pull a bad node; client caches that ignore TTL and open long-lived connections can lag even longer.
a longer TTL means the cache stays stale longer, so updates propagate more slowly, not faster.
TTL directly governs how long clients keep seeing the old record — it strongly affects update speed.
TTL is a DNS record's cache lifetime, unrelated to HTTPS — it affects any traffic relying on it.

scenario: 为 WebSocket 长连接选负载均衡器：同一条连接必须始终落在同一台后端上。
scenario_en: You're picking a load balancer for long-lived WebSocket connections, where a single connection must always land on the same backend.
q: Layer 4 负载均衡器的工作方式是？
q_en: How does a Layer 4 load balancer work?
options: 解析 HTTP 请求内容、按 URL 路径再路由
只做 DNS 解析
工作在传输层：只看 IP/端口做路由
在应用层重写每个请求
why: L4 LB 几乎不拆包，快而高效；建立的 TCP 连接具有粘性（同连接同后端），概念上就像客户端和那台服务器直连——这正是持久连接协议需要的。
why_en: A layer four load balancer routes on IP and port without inspecting content, acting as if the client had a direct persistent TCP connection to one backend.
options_en: It parses HTTP request content and routes on the URL path.
It only does DNS resolution.
It operates at the transport layer, routing only on IP and port.
It rewrites every request at the application layer.

termDefinitions.meaning: OSI 模型里提供端到端保证（可靠性、顺序、流控）的传输层，主角是 TCP/UDP/QUIC。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 4, the transport layer, provides end-to-end guarantees like reliability, ordering, and flow control, dominated by TCP, UDP, and QUIC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

optionExplanations: 解析 HTTP 内容再路由是 L7 负载均衡器的行为，L4 根本不拆包看应用层内容。
DNS 解析是独立的名字服务，跟 L4 负载均衡器转发流量是两个不同的组件。
L4 只看 IP 和端口做路由，几乎不拆包，转发快，同一条 TCP 连接会一直粘在同一个后端。
重写请求内容是应用层（L7）的能力，L4 工作在更底层，看不到也不改应用层数据。
optionExplanations_en: parsing HTTP content to route is L7's behavior — L4 never inspects application-layer content.
DNS resolution is a separate naming service, different from L4 forwarding traffic.
L4 routes only on IP and port, barely inspecting packets, so it's fast and connections stay pinned.
rewriting request content is an L7 capability — L4 operates lower down and can't see it.

scenario: 同一个域名下 /api 要打到服务集群、/static 打到静态集群，必须按路径分流。
scenario_en: Under one domain, /api must route to the service cluster and /static to the static cluster, so routing has to read the path.
q: Layer 7 负载均衡器的工作方式是？
q_en: How does a Layer 7 load balancer work?
options: 原样透传 TCP 数据包、完全不做处理
终止连接，按 HTTP 内容路由
只按源 IP 路由
只能用于 UDP
why: L7 LB 接收的是应用层请求（如 HTTP GET）再转发请求本身：API 请求路由到一组服务器、网页请求到另一组（类似 API 网关），或按 cookie 把同一用户固定到同一后端。
why_en: A layer seven load balancer terminates connections and routes each application-level request based on its content such as URL, headers, or cookies.
options_en: It passes TCP packets straight through, doing nothing to them.
It terminates the connection and routes on HTTP content.
It only routes by source IP.
It only works with UDP.

termDefinitions.meaning: OSI 模型里开发者天天打交道的应用层，跑着 DNS、HTTP、WebSocket 等协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 7, the application layer, is where developers spend their time, running protocols like DNS, HTTP, and WebSocket.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

optionExplanations: 原样透传不处理是 L4 负载均衡器的行为，L7 恰恰要终止连接并解析内容。
L7 负载均衡器要接住完整的应用层请求，再依据其中的路径、cookie 等内容转发给合适的后端组。
只按源 IP 路由信息量太少，L7 能看到的是完整的 HTTP 请求内容，不止是 IP。
L7 是为 HTTP 等应用层协议设计的，这正是它的主场，不是只能用于 UDP。
optionExplanations_en: passing packets through untouched is L4's job — L7 exists to terminate and parse content.
an L7 load balancer receives the HTTP request and forwards it based on content like path or cookie.
routing on source IP alone is too little information — L7 sees the full HTTP request.
L7 is built for HTTP-style protocols — that's its home turf, not something limited to UDP.

scenario: 你的设计用 WebSocket 维持约 500 万条长连接。握手时不需要按 path / header 路由（所有连接都去同一组 chat 后端），TLS 在后端终止，你希望 LB 每条连接的开销尽量小。
scenario_en: Your design keeps about 5 million long-lived WebSocket connections. No path- or header-based routing is needed at handshake time (every connection goes to the same pool of chat backends), TLS terminates on the backends, and you want the LB's per-connection overhead as low as possible.
q: 该选哪种？
q_en: Which load balancer type should you choose for WebSocket traffic?
options: 无所谓，L4 和 L7 在这些约束下开销完全一样
只能靠 DNS 轮转，别无选择
选 L7：它要解析 HTTP 握手并维护两段代理连接，在这里换来的内容路由能力用不上
选 L4：只按 IP/端口把整条 TCP 连接转发到一个后端，不解析内容，每连接开销最小
why: L4 和 L7 都能承载 WebSocket：L7 LB（如 ALB、NGINX、Envoy）处理 Upgrade 握手后同样把这条连接固定到一个后端。本题的关键约束是“握手时不需要看内容、TLS 在后端终止、要最小化每连接开销”，所以不解析 HTTP 的 L4 最合适。若需要按 path / header 路由、在 LB 终止 TLS 或做 WAF，就该选支持 WebSocket 的 L7。
why_en: Both L4 and L7 can carry WebSocket: an L7 LB (ALB, NGINX, Envoy) handles the Upgrade handshake and then pins that connection to one backend too. The deciding constraints here are no content-based routing, TLS terminated on the backends, and minimal per-connection overhead, so an L4 LB that never parses HTTP fits best. If you need path/header routing, TLS termination at the LB, or a WAF, a WebSocket-capable L7 LB is the right pick.
whenOtherWins: 普通 HTTP/REST/SSE 长轮询等流量选 L7：能按内容路由、做 API 网关式的分流。
options_en: It doesn't matter — L4 and L7 have identical overhead under these constraints.
DNS round-robin is the only option.
L7: it parses the HTTP handshake and proxies two connection legs, buying content-routing features you don't need here.
L4: it forwards each whole TCP connection to one backend by IP/port without parsing content, so per-connection overhead is lowest.
tradeoff: L4 持久连接粘性 vs L7 按内容灵活路由

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 4, the transport layer, provides end-to-end guarantees like reliability, ordering, and flow control, dominated by TCP, UDP, and QUIC.

termDefinitions.meaning: OSI 模型里开发者天天打交道的应用层，跑着 DNS、HTTP、WebSocket 等协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 7, the application layer, is where developers spend their time, running protocols like DNS, HTTP, and WebSocket.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上提供持久、双向通信的协议，通过 HTTP upgrade 建立。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that provides a persistent, bidirectional channel over one TCP connection, established via an HTTP upgrade.

optionExplanations: 两种 LB 的每连接开销不同：L7 要解析握手并维护两段连接，在 500 万长连接下差别可观，不是无所谓。
DNS 轮转能分散初始连接目标，但没法在连接建立后感知服务器健康状况，不能替代专门的负载均衡器。
L7 同样能承载 WebSocket（处理 Upgrade 握手后固定到一个后端），但这里用不上它的内容路由，却要多付解析和两段连接的开销。
对：在“握手后不看内容、TLS 在后端终止、要最小化每连接开销”的约束下，只转发 TCP 连接的 L4 最合适。
optionExplanations_en: The two LB types differ in per-connection overhead: L7 parses the handshake and keeps two legs, which matters at 5 million connections, so it is not a free choice.
DNS round-robin spreads initial targets but can't sense health after connecting, no substitute for a real LB.
L7 can carry WebSocket too (it handles the Upgrade handshake, then pins the connection to one backend), but here its content routing goes unused while you still pay for parsing and two legs.
Right: with no content routing after the handshake, TLS on the backends and a need for minimal per-connection overhead, an L4 LB that just forwards the TCP connection fits best.

scenario: 流量里既有要按 URL 分流的 HTTP，也有必须保持连接粘性的长连接，你得选层。
scenario_en: Your traffic mixes HTTP that needs URL-based routing with long-lived connections that need stickiness, so you have to pick a layer.
q: L4 与 L7 负载均衡器的一句话对比是？
q_en: What is the one-line comparison between L4 and L7 load balancers?
options: L4 不看内容快转发；L7 按内容智能路由
L4 才是更智能的那个，反而 L7 转发更快
两者都会终止 TCP 连接
L7 完全不支持 HTTP
why: 一条性能与智能的取舍线：L4 = 只看 IP/端口、开销低，同一条 TCP 连接天然落在同一后端；L7 = 终止连接、按 HTTP 内容路由，代价是解析请求的 CPU。长连接两种都能承载（L7 也支持 WebSocket upgrade 并保持连接粘性），所以按「要不要按内容分流、能否接受解析开销」来选。
why_en: A performance-versus-intelligence tradeoff: L4 looks only at IP/port with low overhead, and a TCP connection naturally stays on one backend; L7 terminates connections and routes on HTTP content at the cost of parsing CPU. Both can carry long-lived connections (L7 also supports WebSocket upgrade with connection affinity), so choose by whether you need content-based routing and can afford the parsing cost.
options_en: L4 forwards fast without looking at content; L7 routes intelligently on content.
L4 is actually the smarter one, while L7 is the faster forwarder.
Both of them terminate the TCP connection.
L7 doesn't support HTTP at all.
tradeoff: L4 快但看不到内容 vs L7 智能但更耗 CPU
