optionExplanations: L4 不解析内容、只按 IP/端口快速转发；L7 会终止连接、解析 HTTP 内容再智能路由——速度与智能的取舍。
这把两者的能力描述对调了——更智能、能看内容的是 L7，转发更快的是 L4。
透传型 L4 通常不终止连接；代理模式的 L4（如 HAProxy TCP mode）会终止 TCP 再新建，属于实现差异，但并不是两者都必然终止——题目问的是它们的核心区别。
L7 恰恰是围绕 HTTP 这类应用层协议设计的，支持 HTTP 正是它的主场能力。
optionExplanations_en: L4 forwards fast on IP/port without parsing content, while L7 terminates and routes on HTTP content.
this swaps the two — L7 is the smarter one that sees content, L4 is the faster one.

A pass-through L4 typically does not terminate the connection; a proxy-mode L4 (e.g. HAProxy TCP mode) does terminate and re-open TCP, an implementation difference, but it is not the case that both always terminate, and this is not the core contrast the question asks about.
L7 is built specifically around protocols like HTTP — supporting HTTP is exactly its home turf.

q: 关于负载均衡器部署在哪里,下面哪个说法对?
q_en: Which statement about where load balancers sit is correct?
options: 负载均衡既用于南北向(客户端↔系统,对外),也用于东西向(服务↔服务,内部);「把请求摊到一组后端」和谁调谁无关
负载均衡器只能放在客户端和系统之间(南北向),内部服务之间用不上
东西向指客户端到服务器,南北向指服务器到服务器
内部服务之间只能点对点直连,不存在负载均衡
options_en: Load balancing is used both north-south (client to system, external) and east-west (service to service, internal); spreading requests across a pool has nothing to do with who is calling whom
A load balancer can only sit between clients and the system (north-south); it is not used between internal services
East-west means client to server, and north-south means server to server
Internal services can only connect point-to-point; there is no load balancing between them
why: 负载均衡的本质是把请求分摊到一组后端，和流量方向无关。南北向是客户端进出系统边界；东西向是内部服务互调，常见形态有 Kubernetes Service、service mesh、内部 LB 或客户端侧 LB。
why_en: Load balancing spreads requests across backend pools, so it applies both at the external north-south edge and on internal east-west service calls.

rows: 公网 LB / API 网关

termDefinitions.meaning: 进出系统边界的流量,即客户端和你的系统之间的通信,通常经过对外的负载均衡器/API 网关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: North-south traffic crosses the system boundary — communication between clients and your system, typically through an external load balancer or API gateway.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统内部服务与服务之间的流量,常经过内部负载均衡、Kubernetes Service 或 service mesh。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: East-west traffic is service-to-service inside the system, usually routed through internal load balancing, a Kubernetes Service, or a service mesh.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个服务挂一个 sidecar 代理,由它统一处理服务间的负载均衡、重试、加密等,是东西向流量的常见方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service mesh attaches a sidecar proxy to each service to handle service-to-service load balancing, retries, and encryption — a common way to manage east-west traffic.

optionExplanations: 对:对外可以分给 Web 层,对内也可以分给某个服务的实例池。
内部调用不是只能直连,通常会先经过服务发现或代理层再选一个健康实例。
说反了:南北向才是客户端↔系统,东西向是服务↔服务。
错:内部大量用负载均衡/服务发现来分摊请求,并非只能点对点直连。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: external web-tier balancing and internal service-pool balancing are the same basic pattern.
Internal services often balance through Kubernetes Services, service meshes, or client-side LB.
Reversed: north-south is client-to-system, and east-west is service-to-service.
Wrong: internal traffic heavily uses load balancing and service discovery to spread requests; it is not limited to point-to-point.

scenario: 凌晨三点一台后端进程假死但端口还在监听，你不想让值班同学被叫醒手动摘流。
scenario_en: At three in the morning a backend process hangs while still holding its port open, and you don't want on-call paged to drain it by hand.
q: 负载均衡器靠什么实现自动故障转移（高可用的关键）？
q_en: How do load balancers implement automatic failover for high availability?
options: 靠人工值守切换
健康检查：主动探测，如请求 HTTP /health 并检查返回
定期把所有后端服务器统统重启一遍
把流量全部缓存起来
why: LB 持续探测后端健康，连续失败就停止路由、恢复后再加回来，全程无需人工。注意本题的假死进程端口仍在监听，单纯 TCP 连接探测会判它「活着」；要用 L7 探测（如 GET /health 要求 2xx 且在超时内返回）才能发现。
why_en: The LB continuously probes backends, stops routing to one after consecutive failures, and adds it back on recovery, with no human needed. Here the hung process still accepts TCP connections, so a plain TCP probe would mark it healthy; you need an L7 probe (e.g. GET /health expecting a 2xx within a timeout) to catch it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    LB["LB"] -->|健康检查| A["Server A OK"]
    LB -->|健康检查失败| B["Server B"]
    B -.摘除.-> X["不接流量"]
    A --> U["用户请求"]
options_en: A human manually flips traffic over.
Health checks: active probes, e.g. requesting HTTP /health and checking the response.
Periodically restart every backend server across the board.
Cache all of the traffic.
codeSample:
GET /health HTTP/1.1
Host: backend-3

HTTP/1.1 200 OK   # 健康，继续接流量
HTTP/1.1 500      # 或超时无响应 -> 摘除该实例

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载均衡器定期探测后端是否存活/正常响应，失败就摘掉流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A health check is the load balancer periodically probing whether a backend is alive and responding correctly, pulling traffic if it fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器、并监控它们健康状态的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer is the component that distributes requests across multiple backend servers and monitors their health.

optionExplanations: 人工值守切换太慢，达不到自动故障转移的要求，这不是负载均衡器实现高可用的方式。
负载均衡器持续主动探测后端，连续失败就停止路由、恢复后再加回来，全程无需人工。本题进程假死但端口仍在监听，单纯 TCP 连接探测发现不了，要用 L7 探测（如 /health 要求 2xx）。
重启所有服务器代价太大也没必要，健康检查只需摘掉出问题的那台，其余不受影响。
缓存流量解决的是重复读请求的问题，跟检测和绕开故障服务器完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: manual on-call switching is too slow to count as automatic failover.

The load balancer keeps actively probing backends, stops routing after consecutive failures and re-adds the backend on recovery, with no human involved. Here the process is hung but still listening, so a plain TCP probe would not catch it; an L7 probe (e.g. /health expecting a 2xx) is needed.
restarting every server is costly and unnecessary — health checks only need to pull the failing one.
caching traffic solves a repeated-read problem, unrelated to detecting a failed server.

q: 补全常见负载均衡算法：
q_en: Fill in the common load-balancing algorithms.
text: {{Round Robin}}：按顺序轮流分发；Random：随机分发；{{Least Connections}}：发给活跃连接最少的服务器；Least Response Time：发给响应最快的；{{IP Hash}}：按客户端 IP 决定服务器，可用于会话保持。
why: 无状态应用用轮询/随机就好——新服务器加入后自然开始分到流量；持久连接服务用最少连接；要会话粘性用 IP Hash。
why_en: Round robin cycles through servers, least connections picks the server with the fewest active connections, and IP hash maps a client to a consistent server for session persistence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定顺序轮流把请求分给每台服务器的负载均衡算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round robin is a load-balancing algorithm that cycles through servers in a fixed order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把新请求发给当前活跃连接数最少的服务器的负载均衡算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Least connections is a load-balancing algorithm that sends each new request to whichever server currently has the fewest active connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按客户端 IP 计算哈希决定路由到哪台服务器的负载均衡算法，可用于会话保持。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP hash is a load-balancing algorithm that hashes the client IP to pick a server, useful for session persistence.

scenario: 你的服务维护大量 SSE / WebSocket 持久连接，担心负载在服务器间越来越不均。
scenario_en: Your service holds many SSE or WebSocket connections, and you are worried that load will drift unevenly across servers.
q: 负载均衡算法该选？
q_en: Which load-balancing algorithm should you choose for many persistent connections?
options: 永远用轮询
IP Hash
最少连接
随机
why: 长连接不像短请求会自然消散：轮询下先起的服务器会一直背着旧连接。按活跃连接数分发能防止单机被长连接慢慢压满。
why_en: For services holding SSE or WebSocket connections use least connections, which prevents one server from gradually accumulating all the active connections.
whenOtherWins: 无状态短请求服务用轮询或随机即可——简单、且扩容加机器后流量自然流向新节点。
options_en: Always use round robin.
IP hash.
Least connections.
Random.
tradeoff: Least Connections 防止长连接堆积 vs Round Robin 简单够用

termDefinitions.meaning: 把新请求发给当前活跃连接数最少的服务器的负载均衡算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Least connections is a load-balancing algorithm that sends each new request to whichever server currently has the fewest active connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按客户端 IP 计算哈希决定路由到哪台服务器的负载均衡算法，可用于会话保持。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP hash is a load-balancing algorithm that hashes the client IP to pick a server, useful for session persistence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定顺序轮流把请求分给每台服务器的负载均衡算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round robin is a load-balancing algorithm that cycles through servers in a fixed order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP 的单向推送标准，服务器在一个长响应里持续发送多条消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE is an HTTP-based standard for one-way server push that streams multiple messages over a single long response.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上提供持久、双向通信的协议，通过 HTTP upgrade 建立。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that provides a persistent, bidirectional channel over one TCP connection, established via an HTTP upgrade.

optionExplanations: 轮询按请求次数平均分配，但长连接不会自然消散，先起的服务器会一直背着旧连接越堆越重。
IP Hash 是为了让同一来源 IP 稳定落到同一后端（如会话粘性），不是用来均衡长连接数量的。
按当前活跃连接数分发，能防止某台服务器因背了太多长连接而被压满，这正是持久连接要解决的问题。
随机跟轮询有同样的问题——不看每台服务器当前背了多少条长连接，容易导致分布不均。
optionExplanations_en: Round robin splits by request count, but long connections don't dissipate, so early servers keep piling up.
IP Hash keeps a source IP on the same backend for stickiness, not for balancing connection counts.
distributing by active connection count keeps one server from being overloaded with too many long ones.
Random shares round robin's blind spot — it ignores current connection counts, so it can end up uneven.

scenario: 你估算下来负载均衡器要扛 500 万 QPS，面试官正盯着这个数字等你回应。
scenario_en: Your estimate puts five million requests per second through the load balancer, and the interviewer is staring at that number waiting for you.
q: 现实中的专用负载均衡器有哪些形态？
q_en: What forms do dedicated load balancers take in practice?
options: 硬件/软件/云三种形态
只有软件一种形态
云负载均衡器无法扩展
硬件 LB 已被淘汰
why: 三种形态：硬件设备（如 F5）、软件（HAProxy、Nginx、Envoy）、云托管（AWS ELB 等）。具体吞吐取决于型号、连接模式、TLS 和 payload，不要背固定数字。估出 500 万 QPS 时，一句「LB 层本身可以横向扩展——DNS/anycast 分到多台 LB，或用云 LB / 高性能硬件」就能体面地带回主线。
why_en: Three forms: hardware appliances (e.g. F5), software (HAProxy, Nginx, Envoy), and cloud-managed (AWS ELB, etc.). Actual throughput depends on model, connection mode, TLS, and payload, so don't memorize a fixed number. At five million QPS, saying "the LB tier scales horizontally too: DNS/anycast across multiple LBs, or a cloud LB / high-end hardware" brings the conversation back on track.
options_en: Hardware, software, and cloud forms.
Only the software form exists.
Cloud load balancers cannot scale.
Hardware load balancers are obsolete.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器、并监控它们健康状态的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer is the component that distributes requests across multiple backend servers and monitors their health.

optionExplanations: 现实里的负载均衡器分硬件、软件、云托管三种形态。
软件负载均衡器（如 Nginx）只是三种形态之一，硬件和云托管产品同样常见。
云负载均衡器（如 AWS ALB）本身就是为弹性扩展设计的，说它无法扩展正好说反了。
硬件 LB 在超大规模、需要极致吞吐的场景仍在用，没有被淘汰。
optionExplanations_en: In practice load balancers come in three forms: hardware, software, and cloud-managed.
a software LB (like Nginx) is just one of three forms — hardware and cloud products are common too.
cloud LBs (like AWS ALB) are literally built for elastic scaling — saying they can't scale is backwards.
hardware LBs are still used at extreme scale where throughput demands are highest.

scenario: 服务要在单个数据中心断电时仍可用，但不想承担跨大洲复制带来的写延迟。
scenario_en: The service must stay available when a single data center loses power, but you don't want to pay the write latency of cross-continent replication.
q: 什么是可用区（availability zone）模式？
q_en: What is the availability-zone deployment pattern?
options: 把所有服务器放在一栋楼里
每个用户一台专属服务器
只在一个国家部署
同区域多个数据中心（AZ）
why: 全球服务的标准拓扑：区域内多 AZ 抗局部灾难，跨城市/大洲复制抗区域故障。但全球部署引出新问题——物理距离带来的延迟。
why_en: A region contains multiple data centers called availability zones so one building failure cannot take down the service, and the model repeats across world cities.
options_en: Put all the servers in one building.
Give every user a dedicated server.
Deploy only in one country.
Multiple data centers, called AZs, within one region.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一区域内彼此独立供电、网络的数据中心，用来抗局部故障。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An availability zone is a data center within a region that has independent power and networking so it can survive a local outage.

optionExplanations: 都放一栋楼没有任何容灾能力，一次停电或火灾就能整体挂掉，跟可用区模式的初衷相反。
每用户一台专属服务器是资源浪费，跟可用区描述的「同区域多机房分布」完全是两码事。
只在一个国家部署跟可用区模式无关，那是「有没有跨区域部署」这个更大的话题。
可用区模式是在同一区域内部署多个物理隔离的数据中心，任何一个 AZ 出问题都不会拖垮整个区域。
optionExplanations_en: one building has zero disaster resilience — one outage takes it all down, the opposite of AZs.
one dedicated server for every single user wastes resources and has nothing to do with what an AZ describes.
deploying in one country is unrelated to the AZ pattern — that's cross-region deployment instead.
the AZ pattern deploys multiple isolated data centers within a region, so one AZ failing doesn't sink it.

q: 光纤中的光速给纽约-伦敦的往返延迟定了什么物理下限？
q_en: What round-trip latency floor does the speed of light in fiber impose between New York and London?
options: 约 1ms
往返理论最低约 56ms
约 500ms
没有物理下限，取决于带宽
why: 纽约到伦敦大圆距离约 5,570km，光纤里光速约 20 万 km/s，单程约 28ms、往返约 56ms。还没算路由绕行和任何处理时间，物理就先收走 56ms——你无法优化光速，这是低延迟应用要做地理分布的根本原因。
why_en: New York to London is about 5,570 km along the great circle, and light in fiber travels about 200,000 km/s, so one way is about 28 ms and a round trip about 56 ms. Before any routing detours or processing, physics already takes 56 ms — you cannot optimize the speed of light, which is why latency-sensitive apps distribute geographically.
scenario: 设计一个跨大陆服务：客户端在纽约，一部分依赖部署在伦敦，链路走海底光纤（光纤中光速约为真空的 2/3），需要估算物理延迟的下限。
scenario_en: You are designing a cross-continent service: the client is in New York, one dependency runs in London, and traffic goes over undersea fiber (light in fiber travels at about two thirds of its vacuum speed), so you need the physical latency floor.
options_en: About 1 millisecond.
The theoretical round-trip floor is about 56ms.
About 500 milliseconds.
There's no physical floor, it's all down to bandwidth.
optionExplanations: 1ms 远低于光速物理下限，这个量级只够本地局域网内往返。
光纤里光速打了折扣，纽约到伦敦的物理距离决定了这个往返下限。
500ms 比物理下限高出一个数量级，那是把网络拥堵也算进去的量级。
距离和光速摆在那儿，物理下限是存在的，不是单纯看带宽。
optionExplanations_en: 1ms sits far below the physical floor — that magnitude only fits a local LAN round trip.
fiber slows light below its vacuum speed, and NY-London distance sets this floor.
500ms is an order of magnitude above the floor — that's counting network congestion too.
distance and light speed are fixed, so a physical floor exists — it isn't just about bandwidth.

scenario: 数据高度可缓存、且全球各地都要查询——比如 Facebook 帖子搜索的热门结果。
scenario_en: The data is highly cacheable and queried globally, such as popular Facebook post search results.
q: 降低延迟的首选策略是？
q_en: What is the first strategy to reduce latency for globally cached data?
options: 把整份数据库都完整复制到每一个国家去
干脆让用户等着
CDN：边缘节点就近命中，卸后端压力
只增加服务器的 CPU
why: CDN 的前提是缓存：数据不常变/不需要频繁更新时就能放到边缘。静态资源（图片、视频）最典型，可缓存的查询结果同样适用——既降延迟又卸后端压力。
why_en: A CDN caches highly cacheable data at edge servers near users, cutting latency dramatically while also reducing load on the backend.
whenOtherWins: 高度动态、按用户各不相同、不可缓存的数据不适合 CDN——这时要靠区域化部署把计算和数据搬到用户附近。
options_en: Fully replicate the entire database into every single country.
Just make the user wait.
A CDN: edge servers serve nearby hits and take load off the backend.
Just add more server CPU.
tradeoff: CDN 缓存可复用内容 vs 区域分区处理动态本地数据

rows: 高度可缓存、少变的内容
按用户地理天然隔离的数据

termDefinitions.meaning: 遍布各地的边缘服务器网络，把可缓存内容放到离用户更近的地方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge servers spread across locations that cache content closer to users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按地理区域拆分数据和服务，让每个区域只处理本地请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Regional partitioning splits data and services by geography so each region only handles its own local requests.

optionExplanations: 把数据库整份复制到每个国家能降延迟，但要处理多地写入一致性，对可缓存的只读查询是杀鸡用牛刀。
让用户干等不是解决方案，只是回避了问题，面试里这个选项本身就不该出现在候选方案里。
数据高度可缓存又要全球访问时，CDN 把内容放到边缘节点就近命中，既降延迟又替源站卸压力。
加 CPU 解决的是计算瓶颈，这里的延迟主要来自网络距离，堆算力对物理传输时间没有帮助。
optionExplanations_en: Fully replicating the database everywhere cuts latency but adds multi-region write consistency — overkill.
Making users wait isn't a solution, it just dodges the problem — shouldn't even be a candidate option.
when data is highly cacheable and globally accessed, a CDN serves it from edge nodes near the user.
Adding CPU addresses a compute bottleneck; the latency here comes from network distance, not compute.

scenario: Uber 式业务：迈阿密的乘客永远不会约纽约的司机——请求天然只关心本地数据。全天有百万级用户，但单个城市内只有几千。
scenario_en: In an Uber-like system, a rider in Miami will never match with a driver in New York; there are millions of users globally but only thousands per city.
q: 架构上该利用这个洞察做什么？
q_en: What architecture should you use when requests naturally only need local data?
options: 区域分区：按城市分数据库，就近处理
把所有数据都集中放进一个全球主库里
每个用户复制全量数据
全部靠 CDN 缓存
options_en: Regional partitioning: split the database by city and handle requests locally.
Concentrate all data into one single global primary database.
Replicate all data to every user.
Rely entirely on CDN caching.
tradeoff: 粗粒度区域路由 vs 细粒度空间索引
why: 先按城市或区域把请求路由到本地分片，再在本地分片里做附近搜索。geohash 没错，但它通常是第二层：用于在迈阿密分片内找附近司机。
why_en: First route the request to the city or regional shard, then run proximity search inside that local shard. Geohash is useful, but usually as the second layer.
whenOtherWins: 若数据必须全球共享（社交关系图、全球排行榜），不能只查本地分片；需要复制、缓存或跨区查询来处理全局视图。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  R["Miami rider request"] --> G["geo/city router"]
  G --> M["Miami regional shard"]
  G -.not needed.-> N["New York shard"]
  M --> H["geohash / spatial index"]
  H --> D["nearby Miami drivers"]

rows: 先决定查哪个本地数据集
在本地数据集中找附近对象
geohash 扫当前格和相邻格
处理城市边界或机场等灰区
额外查相邻区域或相邻格

termDefinitions.meaning: 按城市、州或区域拆数据。请求先被路由到拥有本地数据的分片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Regional sharding splits data by city, state, or region, so a request first reaches the shard that owns the local data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 这里指拥有本地区域数据的服务或数据库分片，不一定真在同一座城市。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A local node means the service or database shard that owns that region's data, not necessarily a machine physically inside the city.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把经纬度编码成网格键。它适合在某个区域内快速找附近对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash encodes latitude and longitude into grid keys, which helps find nearby objects inside a chosen region.

optionExplanations: 请求天然只关心本城市数据时，按城市分库能让绝大多数请求就近处理，而不是每次都跨城市查询。
所有数据挤进一个全球主库会让每个请求都可能跨地域访问，直接违背了「本地请求只关心本地数据」这条约束。
给每个用户复制全量数据既浪费存储也没必要——用户压根不需要其他城市的完整数据。
CDN 适合缓存不常变的内容，这里的乘客-司机匹配数据高度动态、实时变化，不适合靠缓存解决。
optionExplanations_en: when requests only care about their own city, partitioning by city serves most requests locally.
Cramming data into one global primary means any request could cross regions, breaking the locality constraint.
Replicating full data per user wastes storage and isn't necessary — users never need another city's full data.
A CDN suits content that rarely changes; rider-driver matching is too dynamic for caching alone to fix.

scenario: 用户在 LA，核心服务和数据在纽约；即使数据库查询本身很快，跨洲网络距离也会进入端到端延迟。
scenario_en: A user is in Los Angeles while the core service and data are in New York; even a fast database query still pays cross-country network distance.
q: 「数据局部性（data locality）」原则的内容是？
q_en: What does the data locality principle mean?
options: 数据必须始终存放在本机的本地物理磁盘上
整个计算领域通用：数据离计算越近越快
每个国家各存一份数据副本
数据永远只能有一份
why: LA↔NY 约 4,000km，光纤约 200,000km/s，单程物理下限约 20ms、RTT 至少约 40ms；真实路径还会更高。数据局部性就是让一次查询需要的数据彼此靠近，并尽量靠近用户。
why_en: Data locality means keeping query data close together and near the user; LA to New York already has roughly a 40ms round-trip lower bound before routing and queueing.
options_en: Data must always sit on the local physical disk of the same machine.
A principle across computing: the closer data is to the computation, the faster it runs.
Every country needs its own separate data replica.
There can only ever be a single copy of the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让计算需要的数据尽量靠近计算发生的地方（也靠近用户），以降低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data locality means keeping the data a computation needs as close as possible to where the computation runs, and to the user.

termDefinitions.meaning: Round-Trip Time（RTT）：请求从一端到另一端再返回所需的往返时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round-trip time is the time for a request to travel to the other side and for a response to come back.

optionExplanations: 数据局部性讲的是「数据和计算之间的物理/网络距离」，不是特指必须落在本地磁盘。
数据局部性是计算领域的通用原则——数据离用它的计算越近，网络传输时间越短，延迟越低。
每个国家一份副本是数据局部性的一种可能实现手段，但原则本身不要求必须按国家划分。
数据局部性不禁止多副本，恰恰相反，为让数据离各地用户更近，往往需要多份副本或缓存。
optionExplanations_en: data locality is about physical/network distance, not a rule requiring local disk specifically.
data locality is a general computing principle — the closer data sits to compute, the lower the latency.
one copy per country is one possible implementation, but the principle doesn't require it.
data locality doesn't forbid multiple copies — keeping data close to users often needs replicas.

scenario: 你的跨区域调用平时 100% 成功，某天光缆被挖断，大面积超时突然出现。
scenario_en: Your cross-region calls succeed a hundred percent of the time until a fiber cut suddenly causes widespread timeouts.
q: 这次事故暴露的是分布式系统里的哪条错误假设？正确的心态是什么？
q_en: Which false assumption about distributed systems did this incident expose, and what mindset should replace it?
options: 「磁盘容量永远是无限的」
「所有机器的时钟永远都是同步的」
「用户的行为总是理性的」
「网络是可靠的」
why: 光缆被挖断导致的超时，暴露的是分布式计算谬误第一条「网络是可靠的」。时钟不同步也是经典谬误，但与本次事故无关。健壮的设计把失败当常态：超时、重试 + 退避、降级、跨路径冗余。
why_en: Timeouts from a fiber cut expose the first fallacy of distributed computing: "the network is reliable." Clock skew is also a classic pitfall, but it isn't what this incident shows. Robust designs treat failure as normal: timeouts, retries with backoff, graceful degradation, redundant paths.
options_en: "Disk space is unlimited."
"Every machine's clock is perfectly synchronized."
"Users always behave rationally."
"The network is reliable."
optionExplanations: 磁盘容量有限确实要规划，但这不是分布式系统设计里公认最危险的那条假设。
时钟不同步也是经典的分布式谬误，但与本次光缆被挖断的事故无关。
用户行为的不确定性要在产品和校验层面处理，不是这里说的「系统基础设施层面的假设」。
光缆被挖断导致的超时，暴露的正是分布式计算谬误第一条「网络是可靠的」。服务器会崩、比特会被翻转、光缆会被挖断。
optionExplanations_en: Disk capacity being finite is a real planning concern, but not the most dangerous assumption flagged here.
Clock skew is also a classic distributed-systems pitfall, but it is not what this fiber-cut incident shows.
unpredictable user behavior is a product/validation concern, not an infrastructure-level assumption.
Timeouts from a fiber cut expose the first fallacy of distributed computing, "the network is reliable." Servers crash, bits flip, fiber gets cut.

scenario: 下游服务偶发瞬时故障（临时变慢、偶尔超时），面试官问你怎么处理。
scenario_en: A downstream service has transient failures such as temporary slowness or occasional timeouts, and the interviewer asks how you handle them.
q: 面试官在等的「魔法短语」是？
q_en: What magic phrase is the interviewer looking for when downstream calls fail transiently?
options: 重启服务
换一个下游服务
指数退避重试
把超时设成无限大
why: 超时+重试是处理瞬时失败的基本卫生。指数退避给系统喘息、避免重试风暴；这个短语面试官明确在等，senior 级别要能展开讲 jitter。
why_en: Interviewers are often looking for the magic phrase retry with exponential backoff, and senior candidates should be ready to elaborate on adding jitter.
whenOtherWins: 被重试的 API 若非幂等（如扣款），先解决幂等性（幂等键），否则重试会造成重复副作用。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["第 1 次"] -->|失败| B["等 100ms"]
    B --> C["第 2 次"]
    C -->|失败| D["等 200ms"]
    D --> E["第 3 次"]
    E -->|失败| F["等更久"]
options_en: Restart the service.
Switch to a different downstream service.
Retry with exponential backoff.
Set the timeout to infinity.
tradeoff: 立即重试快但可能雪上加霜 vs 退避慢一点但给系统喘息
codeSample:
delay = min(cap, base * 2 ** attempt) + random(0, jitter)
# attempt=0 -> ~100ms, attempt=3 -> ~800ms + 随机抖动
# cap 防止无限拉长；jitter 避免所有客户端同一时刻齐射重试

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次重试失败后把等待时间成倍拉长的策略，给系统恢复的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exponential backoff doubles the wait time after each failed retry, giving the system room to recover.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给重试等待时间加的随机扰动，防止所有客户端同一时刻一起重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Jitter is randomness added to a retry delay so clients do not all retry at exactly the same moment.

optionExplanations: 重启服务是应对进程本身出问题的手段，跟「下游偶发瞬时故障」这种外部依赖抖动没有直接关系。
临时切换下游服务不总是可行（可能没有备选），也没解决「怎么优雅处理瞬时失败」这个通用问题。
超时配合指数退避是处理瞬时失败的标准做法——退避留出恢复窗口、防止重试打成一片，这正是面试官等的关键词。
把超时设成无限大等于放弃超时保护，请求会一直挂着占资源，跟「快速失败、优雅处理」的方向正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Restarting the service fixes a problem in the process itself, unrelated to a downstream dependency hiccup.
Switching downstream isn't always possible, and it doesn't solve handling transient failure in general.
timeout plus exponential backoff is standard hygiene; it avoids a retry storm, the phrase they listen for.
Setting the timeout to infinite gives up timeout protection entirely, the opposite of failing fast gracefully.

scenario: 下游服务已经过载在返回 500，而你的客户端配置的是立即、无限次重试。
scenario_en: A downstream service is already overloaded and returning 500s, while your client is configured to retry immediately and without limit.
q: 重试为什么是「双刃剑」？
q_en: Why are retries a double-edged sword?
options: 大量重试会反复冲击注定失败的请求，加剧问题
重试会导致数据加密直接失败
重试机制只在单机系统里才有效，分布式里没用
重试本身会让单次请求变得更快
why: 对一个已经趴下的服务疯狂重试等于持续补刀。退避把重试的压力摊薄到时间上，把「雪上加霜」变成「给它时间恢复」。
why_en: Aggressive retries can hammer an already failing service and make things worse, which is why backoff waits progressively longer between attempts.
options_en: A flood of retries keeps hammering a request that's doomed to fail, making things worse.
Retries cause encryption to outright fail.
Retry logic only works on single-machine systems, uselessly in distributed ones.
Retries by themselves make a single request faster.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次重试失败后把等待时间成倍拉长的策略，给系统恢复的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exponential backoff doubles the wait time after each failed retry, giving the system room to recover.

optionExplanations: 对一个撑不住的服务持续发起重试，等于不断在它身上补刀，退避就是把这股冲击摊薄到时间线上，给恢复留窗口。
重试跟数据加密是完全不相关的两件事，重试不会影响加密流程。
重试机制在分布式系统里同样常见（甚至更需要），不是单机系统专属的技术。
重试本身不会让单次请求变快，它只是失败后再试一次，整体反而因等待和退避变慢。
optionExplanations_en: hammering an already-struggling service with retries just keeps piling on, turning a hiccup into a collapse.
retries and data encryption are entirely unrelated — retrying doesn't affect the encryption pipeline.
retry logic is just as common (or more needed) in distributed systems, not single-machine-only.
retrying doesn't make one request faster — it just tries again, and overall latency actually grows.

scenario: 一次下游抖动让 10 万客户端同时失败，而它们用的是完全相同的指数退避参数。
scenario_en: One downstream blip fails a hundred thousand clients at the same instant, and they all run identical exponential backoff parameters.
q: 退避策略里为什么必须掺入随机性（jitter）？
q_en: Why must a backoff strategy include jitter?
options: 为了让日志更好看
防止所有客户端同一时刻同步重试
为了绕过限流
随机性能提升单个请求成功率
why: 没有 jitter，指数退避会让所有客户端的重试波峰完美对齐、一次次齐射。加随机把波峰摊平，才真正给系统留出恢复窗口。
why_en: Jitter adds randomness so clients do not synchronize their retries into repeated simultaneous bursts hammering the service like a jackhammer.
options_en: To make the logs look nicer.
It stops every client from synchronizing their retries at the same instant.
To bypass rate limiting.
Randomness improves a single request's odds of success.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给重试等待时间加的随机扰动，防止所有客户端同一时刻一起重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Jitter is randomness added to a retry delay so clients do not all retry at exactly the same moment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次重试失败后把等待时间成倍拉长的策略，给系统恢复的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exponential backoff doubles the wait time after each failed retry, giving the system room to recover.

optionExplanations: jitter 跟日志好不好看没有关系，它是为了打散重试时机，不是格式或美观层面的考虑。
没有 jitter 所有客户端的退避会同步对齐、一次次齐射；加入随机把波峰摊平，真正给系统留出恢复窗口。
jitter 不是用来绕过限流的手段，限流是服务端主动的保护措施，跟客户端加不加随机无关。
jitter 不提升单个请求本身的成功率，它优化的是全体客户端重试请求在时间上的分布。
optionExplanations_en: jitter has nothing to do with how logs look — it's about spreading out retry timing.
without jitter, every client's backoff aligns and fires in waves; randomness flattens those spikes.
jitter isn't a way to bypass rate limiting — that's a server-side protection, unrelated to client randomness.
jitter doesn't improve any single request's odds — it optimizes how retries are spread over time.

scenario: 支付接口因网关超时被客户端重试，但首次请求其实已经在下游扣款成功。
scenario_en: A payment call is retried because the gateway timed out, but the first request had actually already charged the card downstream.
q: 支付接口 charge $10 遇到重试，怎么防止把用户扣成 $20 甚至 $2,000？
q_en: How do you prevent a retried $10 charge from becoming $20 or $2,000?
options: 从源头上直接禁止一切重试行为
要求每次重试之前都必须人工确认
引入幂等键：客户端为这笔支付生成唯一 key，重试时复用同一个 key，服务端靠它去重
在每次扣款成功后都立刻主动发起一笔退款
why: 客户端为每笔逻辑支付生成一个唯一 key（如 UUID），所有重试都带同一个 key；服务端把 key 和处理结果持久化，重复的 key 直接返回第一次的结果，不再扣款。如果真正扣款发生在外部支付处理方，要把同一个 key 透传下去，让下游也能去重。key 不能用「用户 + 日期」这类业务组合，否则同一天的第二笔合法支付会被误判成重复。`Idempotency-Key` 头是常见实现（IETF 草案），不是已发布的 HTTP 标准。
why_en: The client generates one unique key per logical payment (e.g. a UUID) and sends the same key on every retry; the server persists the key with its result and returns the first result for any repeat, without charging again. If the actual charge happens at an external processor, pass the same key downstream so it can dedupe too. Do not build the key from business fields like user + date, or a second legitimate payment on the same day will be rejected as a duplicate. The `Idempotency-Key` header is a common implementation (an IETF draft), not a published HTTP standard.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: pay(key=K)
    S-->>C: timeout
    C->>S: retry pay(key=K)
    S-->>C: 返回同一结果
    Note over S: K 已处理，不重复扣款
options_en: Forbid all retries outright, from the source.
Require manual confirmation before every single retry attempt.
Introduce an idempotency key: the client generates one unique key for this payment and reuses it on every retry so the server can dedupe.
Immediately issue a refund right after every successful charge.
codeSample:
POST /payments HTTP/1.1
Idempotency-Key: 8e3f1c2a-5b7d-4e19-9a60-2c4d8f1b7e35

# key 由客户端按每笔支付生成（UUID），重试复用；服务端记录该 key 的处理结果；同一个 key 重试直接返回首次结果，不再扣款

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识一次请求的唯一键，服务端靠它识别并拒绝重复执行同一请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotency key uniquely identifies a request so the server can recognize and refuse to re-execute a duplicate.

optionExplanations: 禁止重试会牺牲重试本该解决的可用性，遇到偶发网络抖动请求直接失败，不是好方案。
人工确认在真实高并发场景下完全不现实，重试往往是毫秒级的自动行为，等不起人工介入。
客户端为每笔支付生成唯一幂等键，所有重试复用同一个 key，服务端靠它识别「这笔扣款是不是已经处理过」，重复请求也只扣一次款。
扣款后再退款是先犯错再补救，用户体验和资金流都要多绕一圈，不如从源头防止重复扣款。
optionExplanations_en: Banning retries gives up the availability retries exist for — a brief hiccup just fails the request outright.
Manual confirmation is unrealistic at real concurrency — retries fire in milliseconds, no time for a human.
The client generates one unique idempotency key per payment and reuses it on every retry; the server uses it to recognize a charge was already processed, so it only charges once.
Charging then refunding fixes the mistake after the fact, an extra round trip better prevented at the source.

q: 把熔断器（circuit breaker）的工作流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the circuit breaker workflow in the correct order.
steps: 熔断打开期间，请求直接快速失败，不再发起真实调用
持续监控对外部服务调用的失败情况
试探请求成功则闭合电路恢复，失败则继续保持打开
失败超过阈值，熔断器「跳闸」进入 open 状态
超时之后，电路转入 half-open 半开状态
why: 监控 → 跳闸 → 快速失败 → 半开 → 试探定夺。灵感来自电气熔断器：防止级联故障蔓延，并给故障服务恢复时间。
why_en: A circuit breaker monitors failures, trips open past a threshold, fails fast while open, moves to half-open after a timeout, and a test request decides whether to close.
diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Closed: 正常调用
    Closed --> Open: 失败超过阈值，跳闸
    Open --> HalfOpen: 超时后半开
    HalfOpen --> Closed: 试探成功
    HalfOpen --> Open: 试探失败

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控对某依赖的失败率，超阈值后让请求快速失败而不再真的调用，给依赖恢复时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker monitors failures against a dependency and, past a threshold, fails requests fast instead of calling it, giving the dependency time to recover.

scenario: 推荐服务挂了把整个首页拖死，你要让首页在 100ms 内降级返回而不是干等超时。
scenario_en: The recommendation service is down and dragging the whole home page with it, so the page must degrade within a hundred milliseconds instead of hanging on a timeout.
q: 熔断器带来哪些好处？（多选）
q_en: What benefits does a circuit breaker provide?
options: 快速失败：立刻拒绝而不是干等超时，UI 有快速兜底而非挂死
减负：不再向已经挣扎的服务倾泻更多请求
自愈：不放全量流量的情况下自动试探恢复；隔离故障、防止蔓延到整个系统
提升下游服务的最大吞吐量
why: 熔断器的价值：fail fast、给故障服务减压、半开态自动试探、把一处故障圈起来不扩散。它不会让下游更快——只是不再补刀。
why_en: Circuit breakers fail fast, reduce load on struggling services, self-heal by testing recovery, and keep one failure from cascading through the system.
options_en: Fail fast: reject immediately instead of waiting out a timeout, so the UI gets a quick fallback instead of hanging.
Reduce load: stop pouring more requests onto an already struggling service.
Self-heal by automatically probing recovery without full traffic, and isolate the failure so it doesn't cascade through the whole system.
Increase the downstream service's maximum throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控对某依赖的失败率，超阈值后让请求快速失败而不再真的调用，给依赖恢复时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker monitors failures against a dependency and, past a threshold, fails requests fast instead of calling it, giving the dependency time to recover.

optionExplanations: 熔断打开后请求立刻被拒绝，不用干等一个超时周期，UI 能马上展示兜底状态而不是转圈挂死。
熔断打开意味着不再往已经喘不过气的下游倾泻新请求，替它腾出恢复的空间。
半开态会放一小部分流量去试探下游是否恢复，同时把这处故障圈住，不让它蔓延到整个系统。
熔断器不会让下游服务本身处理得更快，它只是不再往下游补刀，跟提升吞吐量是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: once tripped, requests are rejected instantly instead of waiting out a timeout, so the UI shows a fallback.
a tripped breaker means new requests stop piling onto an already-struggling downstream.
half-open state tests a slice of traffic while containing the failure so it doesn't cascade.
a breaker doesn't make downstream process faster — it just stops piling on, a different thing.

scenario: 数据库冷宕机后需要逐实例重启，但应用服务的重试洪峰和用户流量把第一个实例反复压趴（thundering herd）——第一台永远起不来，整库无法恢复。你要在应用服务（调用方）一侧加一个机制。
scenario_en: After a database cold outage, instances must restart one by one, but the application services' retry floods and user traffic keep crushing the first instance (a thundering herd), so it never comes up and the database never recovers. You want to add a mechanism on the application (caller) side.
q: 预防这类级联故障的关键模式是？
q_en: What pattern prevents this cascading failure during database recovery?
options: 干脆再增加更多的重试次数
把数据库连接池的上限再往上调得更大一些
干脆换成一个更快的数据库
熔断器：超阈值后停止真实调用、快速失败
why: 熔断器在失败率超阈值后进入打开态，调用方直接快速失败，不再把重试和用户请求压到正在重启的 DB 实例上；冷却后进入半开态，只放少量探测请求，实例确认能扛住再逐步放量。这样恢复中的实例有喘息空间，不会被 thundering herd 一次次压回去。更多重试、更大连接池只会放大洪峰；换更快的库不解决「恢复期被流量压死」的问题。
why_en: Past a failure threshold the circuit breaker opens, so callers fail fast instead of pushing retries and user requests onto the restarting DB instance; after a cooldown it goes half-open and lets only a few probe requests through, ramping up once the instance holds. That gives the recovering instance breathing room instead of being knocked down again by the thundering herd. More retries or a bigger pool amplify the flood; a faster database doesn't fix being crushed during recovery.
whenOtherWins: 偶发的瞬时失败用「重试+指数退避」就够；熔断器针对的是持续性故障与级联风险。
options_en: Just add even more retries on top.
Turn the database connection pool cap up even higher still.
Just switch over to a faster database.
A circuit breaker that stops real calls and fails fast past a failure threshold.
tradeoff: 持续重试雪上加霜 vs 熔断给恢复窗口

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控对某依赖的失败率，超阈值后让请求快速失败而不再真的调用，给依赖恢复时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker monitors failures against a dependency and, past a threshold, fails requests fast instead of calling it, giving the dependency time to recover.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大量请求或重试同时压向同一个刚恢复/正在恢复的资源，反而把它再次压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A thundering herd is a burst of simultaneous requests or retries slamming a just-recovering resource hard enough to knock it back down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次重试失败后把等待时间成倍拉长的策略，给系统恢复的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exponential backoff doubles the wait time after each failed retry, giving the system room to recover.

optionExplanations: 增加重试在这个场景里只会火上浇油——第一个实例本就被 thundering herd 压垮，更多重试等于更多补刀。
调大连接池能缓一时，但根源是重试洪峰持续冲击刚起来的实例，池子再大也会被同样的洪峰打满。
换更快的数据库不解决「实例刚起来就被流量压趴」这个问题，瓶颈在于流量模式而不是单机性能。
熔断器在错误率超阈值后直接停止真实调用、快速失败，给第一个实例留出不被淹没的启动窗口。
optionExplanations_en: Adding more retries here pours fuel on the fire — the first instance is already crushed by a thundering herd.
A bigger connection pool buys a little time, but a retry storm eventually overwhelms any pool size.
A faster database doesn't fix an instance getting crushed at startup — the bottleneck is the traffic pattern.
once the error rate crosses a threshold, the breaker fails fast, giving the first instance a startup window.

scenario: 你要划定微服务系统里熔断器的安装边界，同时不给无网络的调用增加开销。
scenario_en: You're deciding where circuit breakers belong in a microservice system, without adding overhead to calls that never cross the network.
q: 熔断器适合安插在哪些位置？（多选）
q_en: Where should circuit breakers be placed? (Select all that apply.)
options: 对第三方外部 API 的调用
数据库连接与查询
微服务之间的服务间调用
进程内的纯内存函数调用
why: 原则：凡是跨网络、可能失败或变慢的依赖调用都值得熔断保护——第三方 API、数据库、服务间调用都属于这一类。进程内纯内存计算没有网络故障模式，加熔断器只增加开销。
why_en: Rule of thumb: any dependency call that crosses the network and can fail or slow down deserves a circuit breaker: third-party APIs, databases, and service-to-service calls all qualify. Pure in-process, in-memory calls have no network failure mode, so a breaker there is only overhead.
options_en: Calls to third-party external APIs.
Database connections and queries.
Service-to-service calls between microservices.
Pure in-process, in-memory function calls.
tradeoff: 跨网络易失败的调用要熔断 vs 进程内内存调用不需要

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控对某依赖的失败率，超阈值后让请求快速失败而不再真的调用，给依赖恢复时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker monitors failures against a dependency and, past a threshold, fails requests fast instead of calling it, giving the dependency time to recover.

optionExplanations: 调用不受你控制的第三方 API 时，对方抖动或变慢会直接拖累你的服务，值得用熔断器保护。
数据库连接和查询是典型的跨网络调用，会失败或变慢，熔断器能防止连接池被拖垮的查询占满。
微服务之间的服务间调用跨越网络边界，有失败或变慢的可能，属于熔断器的保护范围。
进程内的纯内存函数调用不跨网络，没有「对方变慢/掉线」这种故障模式，套熔断器只是多余开销。
optionExplanations_en: calling a third-party API you don't control means their hiccups drag your service down too.
database connections and queries can fail or slow down, and a breaker stops queries from hogging the pool.
Service-to-service calls between microservices cross the network and can fail or slow down, so they fall within a breaker's scope.
an in-process, in-memory call never crosses the network, so a breaker there is needless overhead.

scenario: 面向公网的服务,后端实例随流量频繁扩缩容,你需要几秒内让路由跟上实例增减,还要按 URL 路径把请求分到不同后端。
scenario_en: A public-facing service whose backend instances scale up and down constantly; routing must reflect added/removed instances within seconds and split requests by URL path.
q: 该用客户端负载均衡还是专用负载均衡器?
q_en: Client-side load balancing or a dedicated load balancer here?
options: 客户端负载均衡:客户端自己直连后端,省掉那一跳延迟最低
专用负载均衡器:多一跳,换秒级更新和精细路由
DNS 轮转 IP 就够,不必加组件
让每台后端各自随机拒绝一部分请求来分摊负载
why: 专用 LB 夹在客户端和后端之间,每请求多一跳;代价换来的是秒级同步服务器列表、按 path/user 精细路由。公网多变后端值这一跳。
why_en: A dedicated load balancer adds one hop per request, but in return gives second-level server-list updates and fine-grained routing by path or user — worth it when the backend churns.
whenOtherWins: 当客户端可控且数量少(gRPC 内部服务、Redis Cluster 客户端),或客户端海量但能容忍慢更新(DNS)时,客户端负载均衡省掉那一跳更划算。
options_en: Client-side LB: the client connects to backends directly and skips the hop for lowest latency.
Dedicated load balancer: one extra hop for second-level updates and fine-grained routing.
Just rotate IPs with DNS; no extra component needed.
Have each backend randomly reject a share of requests to spread load.
tradeoff: 专用 LB 多一跳但更新快、路由细 vs 客户端 LB 省一跳但更新慢

termDefinitions.meaning: 夹在客户端和后端之间的独立服务器或硬件,集中决定每个请求发往哪台后端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dedicated load balancer is a standalone server or appliance between clients and backends that centrally decides which backend each request goes to.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端自己从服务注册中心拿服务器列表并直连目标,省掉集中式 LB 那一跳。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Client-side load balancing has the client fetch a server list from a registry and connect directly, skipping the hop through a central load balancer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 的系统,常返回轮转的 IP 列表,间接充当一种慢更新的客户端负载均衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS resolves domain names to IPs and often returns a rotated IP list, acting as a slow-updating form of client-side load balancing.

optionExplanations: 客户端 LB 直连确实省掉那一跳、延迟最低,但它靠定期同步列表,更新慢,实例秒级下线时会发给已死实例。
专用 LB 多一跳,换来秒级更新服务器列表和按 path 分流,正好命中频繁扩缩容加路由的需求。
DNS 轮转属于客户端 LB,受 TTL 缓存影响同样更新慢,跟不上秒级实例变化。
随机拒绝不是负载均衡,只会制造错误和重试风暴,不解决路由。
optionExplanations_en: Client-side LB does skip the hop for lowest latency, but it syncs the list periodically, so it lags and may hit instances that just died.
The dedicated LB adds a hop but gets second-level list updates and path-based routing — exactly what fast scaling plus splitting needs.
DNS rotation is client-side LB and is slowed by TTL caching, so it cannot track second-level instance changes.
Random rejection isn't load balancing; it just creates errors and retry storms without solving routing.

scenario: 应用层协议(HTTP)在 user space 处理,下面的 L4/L3 在内核(kernel space)处理。你要加一段经常迭代、按请求内容判断的路由逻辑。
scenario_en: The application layer (HTTP) is processed in user space, while the L4/L3 layers below run in the OS kernel (kernel space). You need to add routing logic that iterates often and inspects request content.
q: 把它放 user space 还是 kernel space,各自的代价是什么?
q_en: Put it in user space or kernel space, and what does each cost?
options: 放 kernel space,因为内核里改路由逻辑最方便最快
放 user space:改起来灵活,代价是比内核处理慢、开销大
两层没区别,放哪都一样
放 kernel space,因为应用层根本无法运行任何自定义路由逻辑
why: 上层(user space)灵活易改,但处理慢、开销大;下层(kernel space)极高效但难改。经常迭代的内容路由放 user space,代价是更慢——这也是 L7 比 L4 灵活却更重的原因。
why_en: User space is flexible and easy to change but slower; kernel space is efficient but hard to change. Frequently-changed routing belongs in user space — the reason L7 is heavier than L4.
options_en: Put it in kernel space, since changing routing logic in the kernel is easiest and fastest.
Put it in user space: flexible to change, at the cost of being slower and heavier than the kernel.
There's no difference between the layers; either is fine.
Put it in kernel space, because the application layer can't run any custom routing logic at all.
tradeoff: user space 灵活易改但慢 vs kernel space 高效但难改

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作系统里运行应用程序的区域,应用层协议在这里处理,灵活易改但每次处理要多绕一圈、更慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: User space is where an OS runs application programs; the application layer is processed here — flexible and easy to change, but slower per operation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作系统内核运行的区域,L4/L3 等底层在这里处理,极高效但代码难改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kernel space is where the OS kernel runs; lower layers like L4/L3 are processed here — very efficient but hard to change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层负载均衡,能看 HTTP 内容做智能路由,跑在 user space,更灵活但更重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: L7 is an application-layer load balancer that inspects HTTP content to route, runs in user space, and is more flexible but heavier.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层负载均衡,只看 IP/端口转发,跑在内核,极高效但路由粒度粗。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: L4 is a transport-layer load balancer that forwards on IP/port only, runs in the kernel, and is very efficient but coarse-grained.

optionExplanations: 反了:内核代码极难改、迭代慢,把常改逻辑塞进内核会拖慢整个开发。
user space 处理灵活可改,适合常迭代的规则;代价是每次处理多绕用户态一圈,慢、开销大。
两层区别正是本题重点:上层灵活慢、下层高效难改,不能混为一谈。
过于绝对:应用层完全能跑自定义逻辑(L7 LB 就是),它只是比内核慢。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: kernel code is very hard to change and slow to iterate, so hot-changing logic there drags down development.
User space is flexible to change, good for often-iterated rules; the cost is extra user-mode processing, making it slower and heavier.
The layer difference is the whole point: upper is flexible but slow, lower is efficient but hard to change.
Too absolute: the app layer absolutely can run custom logic (that's what an L7 LB does); it's just slower than the kernel.

scenario: 团队上 GraphQL,想让前端自由查询、不再为每个新页面改后端。上线后前端开始发各种深层嵌套的宽查询。
scenario_en: A team adopts GraphQL so the frontend can query freely without backend changes per page. After launch the frontend starts sending deeply nested, wide queries.
q: GraphQL 后端这边会付出什么代价?
q_en: What does GraphQL cost on the backend side?
options: 几乎没有额外代价,后端只需照着前端发来的这条查询把它要的那些字段原样返回即可
查询执行成为延迟和复杂度来源：嵌套字段容易触发 N+1 数据访问，要靠批处理、查询深度/复杂度限制和专门优化的 resolver 兜住
前端的查询会自动帮后端做好缓存、限流和鉴权
GraphQL 会自动把后端数据库水平分片扩容,吞吐随之提升
why: 前端灵活查询的代价压在后端：每个嵌套字段都由 resolver 执行，深层宽查询容易变成 N+1 次数据库访问，延迟和负载难以预测。后端要加 DataLoader 式批处理、查询深度/复杂度限制，并为热点形状写专门优化的 resolver——省掉的是「每页一个 endpoint」，不是后端工作量本身。
why_en: The flexibility lands on the backend: every nested field runs through a resolver, so deep, wide queries easily turn into N+1 database calls with unpredictable latency and load. The backend needs DataLoader-style batching, query depth/complexity limits, and specially optimized resolvers for hot shapes; you save per-page endpoints, not backend work itself.
options_en: Almost no extra cost — the backend just returns the fields the frontend asked for.

Query execution becomes a source of latency and complexity: nested fields easily trigger N+1 data access, which takes batching, query depth/complexity limits, and specially optimized resolvers to contain.
The frontend's queries automatically handle caching, rate-limiting, and auth for the backend.
GraphQL automatically shards and scales the backend database, so throughput rises.

termDefinitions.meaning: Facebook 2015 年开源的 API 范式,让前端一次查询精确指定要哪些字段和嵌套对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is an API paradigm open-sourced by Facebook in 2015 that lets the frontend specify exactly which fields and nested objects it wants in one query.

termDefinitions.meaning: 后端为 GraphQL 每个字段编写的取数函数;拼任意查询形状时它容易膨胀成定制代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A resolver is the backend function that fetches data for each GraphQL field; shaping arbitrary queries tends to bloat it into bespoke code.

optionExplanations: 查询要后端真正执行,深层嵌套会放大延迟,并非零成本。
灵活性的账单落在后端：每个嵌套字段都由 resolver 执行，深层宽查询容易变成 N+1 次数据访问，需要批处理、深度/复杂度限制和专门优化的 resolver。
GraphQL 不自带缓存/限流/鉴权,这些仍要后端自己实现,反而更难做统一。
GraphQL 只是查询层,与数据库分片扩容无关,不会自动提升吞吐。
optionExplanations_en: Queries still have to be executed by the backend, and deep nesting amplifies latency — it isn't free.

The bill for flexibility lands on the backend: every nested field runs through a resolver, so deep, wide queries easily become N+1 data access, needing batching, depth/complexity limits and specially optimized resolvers.
GraphQL brings no built-in caching, rate-limiting, or auth; the backend still implements them, and uniformly at that.
GraphQL is just a query layer, unrelated to database sharding or scaling, so it won't auto-improve throughput.

scenario: 内部服务间每秒海量并发短调用，你担心要么为每次调用新建 TCP 连接、要么维护一大堆连接让请求排队。团队已在用 gRPC（跑在 HTTP/2 上）。
scenario_en: A huge volume of concurrent short internal service-to-service calls per second, and you worry about either opening a fresh TCP connection per call or keeping a large pool of connections with requests queuing on each. The team already uses gRPC (which runs on HTTP/2).
q: HTTP/2 的哪个特性让这些并发调用能共享少量持久连接、不必排队或每次重建？
q_en: Which HTTP/2 feature lets these concurrent calls share a few persistent connections without queuing or reconnecting each time?
options: protobuf 二进制编码,让每个请求都能更快地把连接建立起来
多路复用：多个请求作为独立 stream 在同一条持久连接上并发交错
健康检查,自动剔除坏连接
DNS 轮转,把请求分散到多台服务器
why: HTTP/1.1 的 keep-alive 已经能复用连接，但一条连接同一时间只能跑一个请求，并发高时要么排队、要么开很多连接。HTTP/2 多路复用让多个请求作为独立 stream 在同一条连接上并发交错，少量长连接就能扛住海量短调用，省掉反复握手和连接池膨胀。protobuf 只管报文变小，和连接复用是两回事。
why_en: HTTP/1.1 keep-alive already reuses connections, but each connection carries one request at a time, so high concurrency means queuing or opening many connections. HTTP/2 multiplexing runs many requests as independent streams interleaved on one connection, so a few long-lived connections handle huge volumes of short calls without repeated handshakes or pool bloat. Protobuf only shrinks the payload.
options_en: Protobuf binary encoding, which sets up each request connection faster.
Multiplexing: many requests run concurrently as independent streams interleaved on one persistent connection.
Health checks that automatically evict bad connections.
DNS rotation that spreads requests across many servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个请求共享同一条持久连接,不必为每个请求重复建立连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multiplexing lets many requests share one persistent connection so you do not rebuild the connection for each request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持多路复用的 HTTP 版本,gRPC 就跑在它上面以避免每请求重建连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/2 is a version of HTTP that supports multiplexing; gRPC runs on it to avoid rebuilding a connection per request.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 的高性能 RPC 框架,用 HTTP/2 和 protobuf,是二进制协议,比 JSON over HTTP 更快更省。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is Google's high-performance RPC framework using HTTP/2 and protobuf; being binary it is faster and leaner than JSON over HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 的二进制序列化格式,报文比 JSON 小、解析更省 CPU,但不涉及连接复用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Protobuf is Google's binary serialization format; messages are smaller than JSON and cheaper to parse, but it has nothing to do with connection reuse.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接的可靠传输层协议,靠握手建立连接,重建连接有开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented reliable transport protocol whose handshake to open a connection carries overhead.

optionExplanations: protobuf 让报文更小、解析更省 CPU,但它不复用连接,握手开销照旧。
多路复用让多个请求作为独立 stream 在同一条持久连接上并发交错，不必排队也不必开一堆连接，正是 HTTP/2 的关键增量。
健康检查是负载均衡剔除坏后端用的,和连接复用无关。
DNS 轮转决定连哪台服务器,不改变每条连接是否需要重复握手。
optionExplanations_en: Protobuf makes messages smaller and cheaper to parse, but it doesn't reuse connections — the handshake cost stays.
Multiplexing runs many requests as independent streams interleaved on one persistent connection, with no queuing and no pile of connections; that is HTTP/2's key increment.
Health checks are how a load balancer drops bad backends; unrelated to connection reuse.
DNS rotation decides which server you hit, not whether each connection repeats a handshake.

scenario: 长连接代理关闭连接时,客户端已发完数据,但服务器那侧还要再发一阵才收尾,不能一次挥手就同时切断两个方向。
scenario_en: A long-lived proxy is closing a connection: the client is done sending, but the server side still has more to send, so one exchange can't shut both directions at once.
q: TCP 断开为什么要四次挥手而不是两次?
q_en: Why does TCP close with four steps instead of two?
options: 连接两个方向各自独立关闭:一方 FIN 只关自己发送方向,对方可以还没发完数据
四次挥手是历史遗留的协议冗余,现代主流实现基本都跳过后面两步
多出的这两步是协议特意留给中间防火墙设备记录连接日志用的
四次挥手比三次握手多出的这两步,是特意设计来让两端重新协商并交换加密密钥用的
why: TCP 是双向连接:客户端 FIN 只表示「我这边发完了」,服务器可能还有数据在发,所以先 ACK 再自己发 FIN;客户端收到后再 ACK,两个方向各自独立关闭。这比三次握手多一步。
why_en: A TCP connection is bidirectional: the client's FIN only says its own send side is done, so the server ACKs first and sends its own FIN once it's finished — each direction closes independently, one more step than the opening handshake.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: FIN
    S-->>C: ACK
    S->>C: FIN
    C-->>S: ACK
    Note over C,S: 两个方向各自关闭
options_en: Each direction closes independently: one side's FIN only shuts its own send direction, while the other may still have data left to send.
The four-step close is legacy protocol redundancy that most modern implementations skip the last two steps of.
The extra two steps exist specifically to give intermediate firewalls time to log the connection.
The extra two steps beyond the three-way handshake exist to let the two ends renegotiate and exchange encryption keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP 控制标志位,表示发送方这一侧数据已经发完,要求关闭这个方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIN is a TCP control flag signaling that the sender is done sending and wants to close that direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP 控制标志位,确认收到了对方的报文(这里指确认收到 FIN)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACK is a TCP control flag confirming receipt of the other side's segment, here acknowledging a FIN.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议,双向维护状态直到显式关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that keeps bidirectional state until explicitly closed.

optionExplanations: 客户端 FIN 只关自己发送方向,服务器确认后仍可以继续发数据,发完才轮到它发 FIN 关自己那个方向。
四次挥手不是冗余,少了任何一步都会让某一方向的关闭状态不明确,现代实现照样走完四步。
防火墙日志跟挥手步数无关,它旁路监听连接,不需要协议专门为它留步骤。
TCP 挥手是控制连接生命周期的信号,不涉及密钥交换,加密握手是 TLS 的事。
optionExplanations_en: The client's FIN only closes its own send side; the server can keep sending after ACKing, then sends its own FIN once done.
The four steps aren't redundant — skipping one leaves a direction's close state ambiguous; real implementations still run all four.
Firewall logging is unrelated to handshake step count — it observes the connection, not a protocol-reserved step.
TCP's close signals manage connection lifecycle, not key exchange — that's TLS's job, not TCP teardown's.

scenario: 一批后端实例每次重启后 IP 都变了,服务注册表里如果记的是旧 IP,请求会打空。
scenario_en: A batch of backend instances gets a different IP every time it restarts; requests miss if the service registry still holds the old address.
q: 节点 IP 由 DHCP 在开机时动态分配,这对服务发现意味着什么?
q_en: Node IPs come from DHCP dynamically at boot — what does that mean for service discovery?
options: 不能硬编码实例 IP,得靠注册中心/健康检查动态同步最新地址
用了 DHCP,IP 地址就终身固定,硬编码完全没问题
DHCP 只影响客户端设备,服务器一律用静态 IP,不受影响
DHCP 会自动帮你把新 IP 同步进服务注册表,不用额外机制
why: DHCP 在实例启动时动态分配 IP,重启、扩缩容都可能换地址。硬编码或很少刷新的服务器列表一旦遇上换 IP 就会打到失效地址,这正是要靠注册中心/健康检查动态维护列表的原因。
why_en: DHCP hands out IPs dynamically at boot, so restarts and scaling events can change an instance's address; a hardcoded or rarely-refreshed server list goes stale the moment that happens — hence the need for dynamic service discovery.
options_en: You can't hardcode instance IPs; a registry or health checks must keep the address list current.
Once DHCP assigns an IP it never changes again, so hardcoding it is perfectly safe.
DHCP only affects client devices; servers always use a static IP and are unaffected.
DHCP automatically pushes the new IP into your service registry with no extra mechanism needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在设备开机时动态分配 IP 地址的协议,地址可能在下次重启时改变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DHCP is the protocol that dynamically assigns an IP address at boot; the address can change on the next restart.

optionExplanations: 换 IP 是 DHCP 动态分配的常态,注册中心/健康检查负责把最新地址同步给需要路由的一方。
DHCP 恰恰是「动态」分配,重启、迁移、扩缩容都可能拿到新地址,不是终身固定。
服务器同样常用 DHCP 分配的地址(尤其云上自动扩缩容的实例),不是只有客户端设备受影响。
DHCP 只负责分配 IP 本身,不负责把变化通知给服务注册表,这需要单独的服务发现机制。
optionExplanations_en: Changing addresses is normal under DHCP; a registry or health checks are what propagate the current address to routers.
DHCP is dynamic by definition — restarts, migrations, and scaling can all yield a new address, not a permanent one.
Servers, especially auto-scaled cloud instances, commonly get DHCP-assigned addresses too, not just client devices.
DHCP only hands out the address itself; syncing that change into a registry needs a separate discovery mechanism.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["实例开机"] --> B["DHCP 分配 IP"]
    B --> C["注册中心记录地址"]
    C --> D["实例重启/扩缩容"]
    D --> E["DHCP 分配新 IP"]
    E --> F["注册中心/健康检查更新"]
    F -.硬编码就漏掉这一步.-> G["旧地址仍在列表里"]

scenario: 后端进程有时端口还开着、TCP 能连上,但应用逻辑已经死锁,只会回 500。负载均衡器要能识别这种「假活」。
scenario_en: A backend process sometimes still accepts TCP connections while its application logic is deadlocked and only returns 500 — the load balancer needs to catch this fake-alive state.
q: 该用 TCP 健康检查还是 L7 健康检查?
q_en: TCP health check or L7 health check here?
options: TCP 健康检查:只确认端口能建连、三次握手能走完,便宜但测不出应用逻辑是否真的卡死
L7 健康检查:真发 HTTP 请求看状态码,能测出应用层假活,代价是多一次往返
两种检查探测的东西完全一样,挑哪个都不影响结果
干脆不配健康检查,故障早晚会被客户端请求超时自然暴露出来
why: 端口开着但应用死锁只回 500 时,TCP 三次握手照样成功,TCP 检查测不出问题;L7 检查真发 HTTP 请求看返回码,才能抓到这种假活状态,代价是每次探测多一次应用层处理。
why_en: A deadlocked app that still returns 500 still completes a TCP handshake fine, so a TCP check misses it; an L7 check actually sends an HTTP request and inspects the status code, catching that fake-alive state at the cost of an extra application-layer round trip.
whenOtherWins: 后端逻辑简单、连接失败与应用故障几乎总是同时发生时(如纯 TCP 代理),TCP 健康检查更便宜也够用。
tradeoff: L7 更能测出应用层假活但更贵 vs TCP 更省但测不出应用层假死
options_en: TCP health check: only confirms the port accepts connections and the three-way handshake completes, cheap but blind to whether the app logic is actually hung.
L7 health check: sends a real HTTP request and reads the status code, catching an app-level fake-alive state at the cost of an extra hop.
Both checks probe exactly the same thing, so picking either one changes nothing about the outcome.
Skip health checks entirely — a crashed backend will eventually surface through client request timeouts anyway.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接的传输层协议,TCP 健康检查只测试三次握手能否成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol; a TCP health check only tests whether the handshake succeeds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层,L7 健康检查在这一层发真实 HTTP 请求并检查响应内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: L7 is the application layer; an L7 health check sends a real HTTP request there and inspects the response.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载均衡器定期探测后端是否存活/正常响应,失败就摘掉流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A health check is the load balancer periodically probing whether a backend is alive and responding correctly.

optionExplanations: TCP 握手成功不代表应用逻辑正常,死锁进程照样能完成三次握手,这种检查漏掉了假活状态。
真发 HTTP 请求看状态码才能识别「端口开着但应用挂了」,这正是本题场景要防住的问题。
两者测的深度完全不同:一个只看连接层,一个看应用层返回内容,效果并不等价。
等客户端超时发现故障意味着已经有真实用户请求打到坏实例上了,健康检查的价值就是提前拦下这些流量。
optionExplanations_en: A successful handshake says nothing about application logic — a deadlocked process still completes it, so this check misses the fake-alive state.
Sending a real HTTP request and reading the status code is what catches a port-alive-app-dead instance, exactly this scenario's risk.
The two checks probe different depths — one only sees the connection layer, the other sees the actual response — not equivalent.
Waiting for client timeouts means real user requests already hit the bad instance; health checks exist to intercept that traffic first.

scenario: 购物车状态缓存在实例内存里，没有共享会话存储；同一用户的后续请求要尽量落在同一台服务器，否则购物车「丢了」。假设用户会话期间客户端 IP 不变、实例数不变。
scenario_en: Cart state lives only in one instance's in-memory cache with no shared session store; a user's later requests should keep landing on the same server or the cart 'disappears'. Assume the client IP and the instance count stay the same during a session.
q: 负载均衡算法该选?
q_en: Which load-balancing algorithm fits here?
options: Least Connections:按当前活跃连接数分发,连接最少的服务器优先接
Round Robin:按固定顺序轮流把请求分给每台服务器
IP Hash:按客户端 IP 算哈希决定服务器,同一来源稳定落在同一台
Random:完全随机地把请求分发给某一台服务器
why: 在客户端 IP 和实例数都不变的前提下，IP Hash 让同一来源稳定落到同一台实例，提供会话粘性；其余三种只管均衡分发，不保证同一用户落在同一台。注意它的边界：IP 一变或扩缩容就会换机器，更稳的做法是 cookie 粘性或把购物车放进共享存储。
why_en: Given a stable client IP and a fixed instance count, IP hash keeps the same source on the same instance, providing session stickiness; the other three only balance load with no such guarantee. Its limit: an IP change or a scaling event moves the user, so cookie-based stickiness or a shared session store is more robust.
whenOtherWins: 如果会话状态存在外部共享存储(如 Redis)而不是实例内存,就不需要粘性,换回 Round Robin/Least Connections 更简单均衡。
tradeoff: IP Hash 保证会话粘性 vs 其他算法分布更均衡但不粘
options_en: Least connections: distributes by current active connection count, the least-busy server gets the next request.
Round robin: cycles through every server in a fixed, repeating order.
IP hash: hashes the client IP to pick a server, so the same source lands on the same backend.
Random: distributes each request to a completely random server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按客户端 IP 计算哈希决定路由到哪台服务器的负载均衡算法,可用于会话保持。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP hash is a load-balancing algorithm that hashes the client IP to pick a server, useful for session persistence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把新请求发给当前活跃连接数最少的服务器的负载均衡算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Least connections sends each new request to whichever server currently has the fewest active connections.

optionExplanations: 按连接数均衡跟「同一用户落在同一台」是两回事,连接数最少的那台不一定是存着这个用户购物车的那台。
轮询只管顺序分发请求次数,完全不看请求来自谁,做不到会话粘性。
按客户端 IP 哈希后路由,同一来源的请求算出的哈希值相同,天然稳定落在同一台实例上。
随机分发跟轮询一样不看请求来源,下一次请求大概率落到别的实例,购物车状态对不上。
optionExplanations_en: Balancing by connection count is unrelated to landing the same user on the same server — the least-busy one may not hold their cart.
Round robin only cycles by request order and ignores where a request came from, so it can't provide stickiness.
Hashing the client IP gives the same source the same hash value, so it naturally lands on the same instance every time.
Random distribution ignores origin just like round robin, so the next request likely lands elsewhere and the cart mismatches.

scenario: 一条 TCP 连接里,接收端处理慢、缓冲区快满了;另一条连接里,中间路由器已经开始丢包拥堵。这是两种不同的信号。
scenario_en: On one TCP connection the receiver is slow and its buffer is nearly full; on another, an intermediate router is already dropping packets under congestion — two different signals.
q: TCP 分别用什么机制应对这两种情况?
q_en: What TCP mechanism handles each of these two situations?
options: 流量控制应对接收方缓冲区快满;拥塞控制应对网络拥堵,两者独立调节发送速率
都是拥塞控制的职责,流量控制只是它的别名
只有拥塞控制存在,TCP 不管接收方处理能力
流量控制和拥塞控制都是由应用层代码手动实现的,TCP 协议本身完全不管
why: 流量控制盯着接收方的缓冲区,防止发送方把接收方冲垮;拥塞控制盯着网络路径,发现丢包或延迟就放慢发送速率给网络喘气。两者信号来源不同、调节目标也不同,常被工程师混为一谈。
why_en: Flow control watches the receiver's buffer so the sender doesn't overrun it; congestion control watches the network path and slows down on loss or delay. They react to different signals even though both throttle the sender.
options_en: Flow control handles a full receiver buffer; congestion control handles network congestion — two independent throttles.
Both are congestion control's job; flow control is just another name for it.
Only congestion control exists; TCP doesn't account for receiver processing capacity at all.
Both flow control and congestion control are hand-implemented in application code; TCP itself does neither.

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP 防止发送方把接收方缓冲区冲垮的机制,盯着接收端处理能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flow control is the TCP mechanism that stops the sender from overrunning the receiver's buffer, tracking the receiver's capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP 根据网络丢包/延迟动态调整发送速率的机制,盯着网络路径本身。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Congestion control is the TCP mechanism that adjusts send rate based on network loss or delay, tracking the path itself.

optionExplanations: 接收方快撑不住是流量控制管的事,网络本身拥堵是拥塞控制管的事,是两套独立机制,不是同一件事的两个名字。
两者信号来源完全不同:一个看接收方缓冲区剩余空间,一个看网络路径的丢包/延迟,不能互相替代。
TCP 明确把「接收方处理能力」和「网络拥堵」拆成流控和拥塞控制两套机制,不是只有一套。
流量控制和拥塞控制都内建在 TCP 协议实现里(操作系统内核层面),不需要应用层代码自己实现。
optionExplanations_en: A slow receiver is flow control's job, network congestion is congestion control's job — two distinct mechanisms, not one thing under two names.
The two watch entirely different signals: one tracks receiver buffer space, the other tracks path loss and delay — not interchangeable.
TCP explicitly splits 'receiver capacity' from 'network congestion' into flow control and congestion control, not a single mechanism.
Both flow control and congestion control are built into the TCP implementation (OS kernel level), not something application code hand-rolls.

scenario: 一对一视频通话中,某个视频帧因网络抖动丢了,等它重传到达时,该播放的已经是下一帧了。
scenario_en: In a one-to-one video call, a frame is lost to jitter, and by the time a retransmit would arrive the next frame should already be playing.
q: WebRTC 音视频流为什么选 UDP 而不是像 HTTP 那样用 TCP?
q_en: Why does WebRTC send audio and video over UDP instead of TCP like HTTP does?
options: 实时音视频要的是新鲜度不是完整性:丢帧直接跳过好过等重传,TCP 的可靠重传反而会让画面卡在等一个丢包上
UDP 头部只有 8 字节,比 TCP 的 20-60 字节更省流量,省下的带宽才是它被选中的真正原因
音视频数据必须无损到达,TCP 更适合,只是浏览器实现选错了协议
WebRTC 的媒体数据其实都经中心服务器转发,不涉及不可靠传输的取舍
why: UDP 不保证送达和顺序,换来的是低延迟——这正是实时音视频要的:一帧迟到的画面不如直接丢弃、播放最新的。TCP 的可靠重传和保序会让整条流卡在等一个丢包上,对实时性是灾难。
why_en: UDP drops delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for low latency, which is exactly what real-time media needs — a late frame is worse than a dropped one. TCP's retransmission and ordering would stall the whole stream waiting on one lost packet.
tradeoff: UDP 低延迟但可能丢帧 vs TCP 完整但可能卡顿等重传
options_en: Real-time media needs freshness, not completeness: skipping a dropped frame beats waiting for a retransmit, which would stall playback.
UDP's header is only 8 bytes versus TCP's 20-60, saving bandwidth — that saved bandwidth is the real reason it was picked.
Media must arrive lossless, so TCP would actually fit better; the browser implementation just picked the wrong protocol.
WebRTC media is actually relayed entirely through a central server, so the unreliable-transport tradeoff doesn't apply.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议,不保证送达或顺序,换取更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让浏览器之间直接进行点对点音视频/数据传输的协议族,媒体走 UDP。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite for direct peer-to-peer audio, video, or data between browsers, with media carried over UDP.

optionExplanations: 丢帧直接跳过、播放最新画面,比等 TCP 重传旧帧更符合实时体验,这是选 UDP 的核心原因。
头部省流量是真的,但只是个小副作用,不是 WebRTC 选 UDP 的原因——真正原因是避免重传拖慢实时性。
把方向说反了:正是因为不想为了「无损」牺牲实时性,才选了容忍丢包的 UDP,不是协议选错了。
WebRTC 的媒体流恰恰是点对点直连、不经中心服务器转发,这也是为什么丢包问题必须靠 UDP 的取舍正面处理。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping a dropped frame and playing the latest one beats waiting on a TCP retransmit — that's the real reason for choosing UDP.
The header savings are real but a minor side effect, not the reason WebRTC picked UDP — the real reason is avoiding retransmit-induced delay.
This reverses the logic: UDP was chosen precisely to avoid sacrificing real-time responsiveness for losslessness, not a mistaken pick.
WebRTC media is exactly peer-to-peer, not relayed through a central server, which is why the packet-loss tradeoff has to be handled head-on with UDP.

scenario: 客户端负载均衡下新加了 3 台实例，它们已通过健康检查、在注册中心标记为可用，而且一部分客户端已经在往它们发请求；但另一些客户端要过十几秒才开始往新实例发请求。
scenario_en: Under client-side load balancing, three new instances were added; they have passed health checks and are marked available in the registry, and some clients are already sending to them. Other clients only start sending to them after a dozen-plus seconds.
q: 为什么新实例没有立刻收到流量?
q_en: Why don't the new instances receive traffic right away?
options: 客户端要等下一次轮询周期,或等注册中心推送到位,列表才会更新
因为新实例本身还在预热,跟客户端负载均衡的更新机制无关
因为新实例的健康检查还没通过,跟客户端负载均衡的更新机制无关
客户端负载均衡不存在这种延迟,新实例加入是瞬时同步的
why: 新实例已健康、已注册，且已有客户端在打它们，说明问题不在实例本身（排除 B/C），而在落后的那些客户端的本地列表。客户端要么定期轮询注册中心、要么等推送，两种方式都有延迟，列表刷新那一刻才开始给新实例发流量。
why_en: The new instances are healthy, registered, and already serving some clients, so the instances themselves aren't the problem (ruling out B/C); the lagging clients' local lists are. Clients either poll the registry on an interval or wait for a push, and either way the update isn't instantaneous: traffic only starts once each client's list refreshes.
options_en: The client waits for the next poll cycle, or for the registry to push the change, before its list updates.
The new instances are still warming up, unrelated to the client-side load-balancing update mechanism.
The new instances haven't passed health checks yet, unrelated to the client-side load-balancing update mechanism.
Client-side load balancing has no such delay; new instances sync instantly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录当前有哪些可用服务器实例及其地址的目录服务,客户端从这里刷新列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service registry is the directory service tracking available server instances, which clients refresh their list from.

optionExplanations: 客户端负载均衡靠定期轮询或被动推送来同步服务器列表,这个刷新周期正是「延迟收到流量」的直接原因。
预热是另一个真实问题,但本题问的是「为什么没立刻收到流量」,根源在列表还没刷新,不在预热。
健康检查确实存在,但本题场景里问题出在客户端列表本身还没更新,不是健康检查没通过。
客户端负载均衡恰恰存在这种同步延迟,不管靠轮询还是推送,都不是瞬时的。
optionExplanations_en: Client-side load balancing syncs its server list via periodic polling or pushed updates, and that refresh cycle is the direct cause of the delay.
Warm-up is a separate real issue, but the question asks why traffic doesn't arrive at all yet — the cause is the stale list, not warm-up.
Health checks are real, but here the client's own list simply hasn't refreshed yet — it isn't a failed health check.
Client-side load balancing does have this sync delay, whether by polling or pushing — it's never instantaneous.

    B --> C{"客户端怎么知道?"}
    C -->|轮询周期到| D["客户端拉取新列表"]

scenario: 用户已登录、token 有效,但访问的是别人的私有相册,接口该返回 401 还是 403?
scenario_en: A user is logged in with a valid token but requests someone else's private album — should the API return 401 or 403?
q: 401 和 403 的语义区别是什么?
q_en: What's the semantic difference between 401 and 403?
options: 401 是没认证/认证失败;403 是认证通过但没权限,已登录访问他人内容该回 403
401 和 403 语义上完全相同,两个状态码可以在任何地方随意互换使用
401 对应的是服务器自身处理请求时发生了错误,403 对应的是客户端本地网络连接出了问题
401 表示资源已经被永久删除,403 表示资源目前临时不可用
why: 401 Unauthorized 是「你还没证明自己是谁」;403 Forbidden 是「你已经证明了,但这件事就是不让你做」。已登录用户访问他人私有相册是认证成功、只是没权限,该回 403;回 401 会误导客户端去重新登录。
why_en: 401 Unauthorized means the server doesn't know who you are yet; 403 Forbidden means it knows and still says no. A logged-in user hitting someone else's private album is authenticated but unauthorized, so the right response is 403, not 401.
options_en: 401 is unauthenticated; 403 is authenticated but unauthorized — a logged-in user viewing someone else's content should get 403.
401 and 403 mean exactly the same thing, so the two status codes can be swapped freely.
401 corresponds to an error the server hit while processing the request, 403 corresponds to a local client-side network connectivity problem.
401 means the resource has been permanently deleted, 403 means the resource is currently temporarily unavailable.

termDefinitions.meaning: Unauthorized:请求缺少有效身份凭证,服务器还不知道你是谁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 401 Unauthorized means the request lacks valid credentials — the server doesn't know who you are yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: Forbidden:身份已确认,但没有权限执行这个操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 403 Forbidden means identity is confirmed, but you lack permission for this action.

optionExplanations: 401 卡在「你是谁都不知道」,403 卡在「知道你是谁但不让你做」,已登录访问他人内容属于后者。
两者语义完全不同,混用会误导客户端做出错误反应(比如让已登录用户去重新登录)。
两者都是客户端错误(4xx),跟服务器自身出错或网络问题无关,那是 5xx 和连接层的事。
资源被删除对应的是 404,资源临时不可用通常对应 503,跟 401/403 的认证-授权语义无关。
optionExplanations_en: 401 is stuck at 'who are you', 403 is stuck at 'we know who you are but say no' — a logged-in user hitting another's content is the latter.
The two mean different things, and conflating them misleads the client into the wrong response, like re-prompting login when already logged in.
Both are client errors (4xx), unrelated to the server's own failures or network issues, which fall under 5xx or the connection layer.
A deleted resource maps to 404, and temporary unavailability usually maps to 503 — neither matches 401/403's authn-vs-authz meaning.

scenario: 服务前面有一层反向代理（如 NGINX），凌晨报警显示大量 5xx。你要先判断错误是你的应用在处理请求时自己报出来的，还是反向代理根本没从你的应用拿到有效响应。
scenario_en: A reverse proxy (e.g. NGINX) sits in front of your service, and an alert shows a spike of 5xx errors. You need to tell whether your application generated the error while handling the request, or the proxy never got a valid response from your application at all.
q: 收到 500 还是 502,分别该往哪查?
q_en: Where do you look first for a 500 versus a 502?
options: 500：应用自己处理请求时出错，查应用日志和异常栈；502：反向代理没从你的应用拿到有效响应，先查应用进程是否崩溃、未监听、连接被重置
500 和 502 其实是同一件事,只是不同框架各自的命名习惯不同
500 是底层网络传输层出现的错误,和应用代码完全无关;502 才是应用代码自己抛出的异常
502 只会出现在客户端断网时,和服务器状态无关
why: 500 Internal Server Error 是生成响应的那台服务器（你的应用）在处理请求时出错，反向代理只是透传。502 Bad Gateway 是网关/代理从它访问的 upstream 收到了无效响应——在这里 upstream 就是你的应用，所以先看应用进程是否挂了、没在监听、连接被重置。你的应用自己调用的下游依赖出错，通常表现为应用返回 500（或应用自身作为网关时返回 502/504）。
why_en: 500 Internal Server Error means the server that generated the response (your application) failed while handling the request; the proxy just passes it through. 502 Bad Gateway means the gateway/proxy got an invalid response from its upstream; here the upstream is your application, so first check whether the app process crashed, isn't listening, or reset the connection. A failure in a dependency your app calls usually surfaces as your app returning 500 (or 502/504 if your app itself acts as a gateway).
options_en: 500: your application errored while handling the request; check app logs and stack traces. 502: the proxy got no valid response from your application; first check whether the app process crashed, isn't listening, or reset the connection.
500 and 502 actually mean the same thing, just different naming conventions across frameworks.
500 is an error at the underlying network transport layer, unrelated to application code; 502 is the one application code itself throws.
502 only happens when the client loses network connectivity, unrelated to server state.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server Error:服务器自己在处理请求时遇到了错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 500 Server Error means the server itself hit an error while handling the request.

termDefinitions.meaning: Bad Gateway:网关/代理本身没问题,但它请求的上游服务器返回了无效响应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 502 Bad Gateway means the gateway itself is fine, but the upstream server it queried returned an invalid response.

optionExplanations: 500 指向应用自己处理请求时的逻辑错误；502 指向反向代理没从它的 upstream（你的应用）拿到有效响应，先看应用进程是否挂了、没在监听、连接被重置，两条排查路径完全不同。
两个状态码的责任方不同(自己 vs 上游),不是命名习惯差异,排查时不能当成一回事。
把责任方说反了:500 恰恰是应用代码/服务器自身出错,502 才是网关拿到了上游的无效响应。
502 描述的是网关和上游服务器之间的响应问题,跟客户端本地是否断网没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: 500 points at the application's own error while handling a request; 502 points at the proxy getting no valid response from its upstream (your application), so first check whether the app process crashed, isn't listening, or reset the connection; the two debugging paths differ.
The two codes name different responsible parties (self vs. upstream), not a naming-convention quirk — they shouldn't be treated as one thing.
This reverses responsibility: 500 is exactly the app/server's own error, while 502 is the gateway receiving a bad upstream response.
502 describes a problem between the gateway and upstream server, unrelated to whether the client itself lost network connectivity.

scenario: 一个 user 拥有多篇 posts，你要在 REST API 里按常见的资源建模惯例表达这种一对多的从属关系。
scenario_en: A user owns many posts, and you need to express that one-to-many ownership relationship in a REST API following common resource-modeling conventions.
q: 按常见 REST 资源建模惯例，怎么表达「一个 user 有多篇 posts」？
q_en: Under common REST resource-modeling conventions, how do you express 'a user has many posts'?
options: 嵌套路径:GET /users/{id}/posts,路径本身表达从属关系
单独开一个 POST /getUserPosts 端点,把 userId 放进请求体
把 posts 整个内嵌进 user 资源的每次响应里,不单独暴露
用一个不带路径参数的全局 /posts 端点,靠客户端自己过滤
why: 常见的 REST 资源建模惯例用嵌套路径表达从属关系：GET /users/{id}/posts，一眼就能读出「这个用户的 posts」。这是惯例而不是 REST 约束本身——GET /posts?userId={id} 这种服务端过滤也是合理设计。B 把动作塞进端点名，是 RPC 风格；C 无法单独分页和寻址；D 把过滤推给客户端，浪费带宽。
why_en: The common REST resource-modeling convention expresses ownership with a nested path: GET /users/{id}/posts reads as this user's posts. It's a convention, not a REST constraint itself; server-side filtering like GET /posts?userId={id} is also reasonable. B stuffs the action into the endpoint name (RPC style); C can't be paginated or addressed on its own; D pushes filtering to the client and wastes bandwidth.
options_en: A nested path: GET /users/{id}/posts, where the path itself expresses the ownership relationship.
A dedicated POST /getUserPosts endpoint, with userId placed in the request body.
Embed posts entirely inside every user resource response, without exposing them separately.
A global /posts endpoint with no path parameter at all, leaving filtering to the client.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把系统建模成「资源」、用标准 HTTP 方法和路径操作它们的 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that models a system as resources manipulated with standard HTTP verbs and path conventions.

optionExplanations: 嵌套路径把从属关系直接编码进 URL,客户端不用查文档就知道这是「这个用户的 posts」。
getUserPosts 是把动作塞进接口名字的 RPC 写法,资源和操作没有分离,不是资源建模。
把 posts 强行塞进 user 响应里,想单独只要 posts 列表时反而绕不开完整的 user 对象。
不带路径参数就丢了「属于哪个 user」这层语义,只能把全量 posts 拉回来自己在客户端筛。
optionExplanations_en: A nested path encodes the ownership relationship directly in the URL — no docs needed to know it's this user's posts.
getUserPosts stuffs the action into the endpoint name, RPC-style, without separating resource from operation.
Forcing posts inside every user response makes it impossible to fetch just the post list without the full user object.
A path-less endpoint drops the 'belongs to which user' semantics, forcing the client to pull everything and filter locally.

scenario: 你把一个只读 GET 接口的旧路径永久迁移到了新路径，同时另一个 GET 接口只是短暂维护、临时跳转到备用地址。
scenario_en: You've permanently migrated an old read-only GET endpoint path to a new one, while a different GET endpoint is only briefly redirecting to a backup during maintenance.
q: 301 和 302 该分别用在什么场景?
q_en: When should you use 301 versus 302?
options: 301 用于永久迁移,客户端/缓存应记住新地址;302 用于临时跳转,下次还应请求原地址
301 和 302 说的其实是同一种永久迁移状态,数字不同只是历史命名习惯没有实际区别
301 用于服务器临时维护期间的跳转,302 用于标记资源已经被永久删除
两者都只影响浏览器地址栏显示,不影响客户端后续该往哪发请求
why: 301 告诉客户端和缓存「这个地址永久搬走了，以后直接用新地址」（301 默认可被缓存）；302 告诉它「这次临时去那边，下次还是先请求原地址」。GET 接口的永久迁移用 301，短暂维护跳转用 302。注意：如果是 POST/PUT 等非 GET 接口，301/302 可能被客户端改成 GET 重发，应改用 308（永久）/307（临时）保留方法和请求体。
why_en: A 301 tells clients and caches the address moved for good, so use the new one from now on (301 is heuristically cacheable); a 302 says this redirect is temporary, keep hitting the original URL next time. Use 301 for a permanent GET endpoint migration and 302 for a temporary maintenance redirect. For non-GET endpoints like POST/PUT, clients may switch 301/302 to GET, so use 308 (permanent) / 307 (temporary) to preserve the method and body.
options_en: 301 for a permanent move that clients/caches should remember; 302 for a temporary redirect where the original URL should still be used next time.
301 and 302 actually both describe the same permanent-move state; the different numbers are just a naming-convention leftover with no real distinction.
301 is for a temporary redirect during server maintenance, 302 is for marking a resource as permanently deleted.
Both only affect what the browser address bar shows, not which URL the client should request afterward.

termDefinitions.meaning: Moved Permanently:资源永久搬到了新地址,客户端和缓存应更新记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 301 Moved Permanently means the resource moved for good; clients and caches should update their records.

termDefinitions.meaning: Found:资源临时跳转到别处,下次仍应请求原地址。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 302 Found means a temporary redirect; the original URL should still be requested next time.

optionExplanations: 301 让客户端和搜索引擎更新书签/索引指向新地址,302 保留原地址下次继续被请求,分别对应永久迁移和临时跳转。
两者语义相反:一个说「以后都用新地址」,一个说「这次临时去那边」,数字差异正对应这层区别。
把场景说反了:永久删除对应的是 410/404 一类,301/302 描述的是「地址搬没搬家」,不是维护或删除状态。
状态码会实际改变客户端(包括程序化客户端、爬虫、缓存)后续请求的目标地址,不只是浏览器地址栏的显示。
optionExplanations_en: 301 makes clients and search engines update bookmarks and indexes to the new address, 302 keeps the original address requested next time — permanent vs temporary.
The two mean opposite things: one says 'always use the new address from now on', the other says 'just this once' — the numbers track that distinction.
This flips the scenarios: permanent deletion maps to 410/404-style codes; 301/302 describe whether the address itself moved, not maintenance or deletion.
Status codes actually change where clients — including programmatic ones, crawlers, and caches — send future requests, not just what a browser's address bar shows.
